subject: Anatomy
stem: The acrosomal cap of the spermatozoon is derived from the
explanation:
During spermiogenesis the Golgi forms the acrosome, the centriole forms the axoneme of the tail, and mitochondria wrap round the middle piece.
> `GENERAL EMBRYOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (mitochondria in middle piece), 2020 INI-CET (spermatogenesis sequence)

subject: Anatomy
stem: The remnant of the notochord in the adult is the
options: Apical ligament of the dens only
explanation:
The notochord forms from cells moving in through the primitive node. Elsewhere it regresses. Its remnants can give rise to a chordoma (typically at the clivus or sacrum).
> `GENERAL EMBRYOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (sacrococcygeal teratoma — primitive streak), 2022 INI-CET (epiblast migration)

subject: Anatomy
stem: Which of the following is derived from paraxial mesoderm?
explanation:
Paraxial mesoderm forms somites, which become sclerotome (vertebrae and ribs), myotome (skeletal muscle) and dermatome (dermis of the back). The kidney is intermediate mesoderm; the spleen and heart are lateral plate (splanchnic) mesoderm.
> `GENERAL EMBRYOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (para-axial mesoderm gives rise to …)

subject: Anatomy
stem: The anterior (cranial) neuropore normally closes at about
explanation:
The posterior (caudal) neuropore closes at about day 28. Failure gives anencephaly (anterior) or spina bifida (posterior). The heart starts beating at about day 21–22.
> `GENERAL EMBRYOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (first heartbeat — 21–22 days), 2016 AIIMS (neuronal migration)

subject: Anatomy
stem: The mechanoreceptor that responds best to vibration and lies in the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue is the
explanation:
Meissner's corpuscles (light touch) lie in the dermal papillae. Merkel's discs (sustained pressure) lie in the basal epidermis. Ruffini endings (stretch) lie in the dermis.
> `GENERAL HISTOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (Meissner's — papillary dermis), 2023 INI-CET (dense irregular CT — dermis)

subject: Anatomy
stem: Pancreatic acinar tissue differs from the parotid gland under the microscope by having
options: Centroacinar cells and no striated ducts
explanation:
Centroacinar cells (the start of the intercalated duct inside the acinus) are unique to the pancreas, which also lacks striated ducts. The parotid has prominent striated ducts and myoepithelial cells. Mucous acini with demilunes are typical of the submandibular gland.
> `GENERAL HISTOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (difference between exocrine pancreas and parotid), 2023 NEET-PG (islets)
exam: 2020 INI-CET (difference between exocrine pancreas and parot

subject: Physiology
stem: The surface tension of the alveolar lining fluid is LOWEST at
options: The end of a normal inspiration
explanation:
As the alveolus shrinks, surfactant molecules are packed more densely and surface tension falls sharply. This keeps small alveoli from collapsing. *Note: the 2024 INI-CET key says surface tension "increases during expiration"; standard texts (Guyton, Ganong) show it falls as alveolar area falls.*
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (surface tension during expiration), 2018 NEET-PG (RDS)

subject: Physiology
stem: On the pressure–volume curve of an isolated lung, at the same transpulmonary pressure the lung volume is
options: Greater during inflation than during deflation
Greater during deflation than during inflation
The same during inflation and deflation
Greater during inflation only if the lung is saline-filled
explanation:
This is hysteresis. Surfactant is spread more effectively during deflation, so less pressure holds a given volume. A saline-filled lung has no air–liquid interface and shows almost no hysteresis.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (hysteresis — surfactant, 3X)

subject: Physiology
stem: Two alveoli connected to the same airway have equal surface tension, but one has half the radius of the other. If there is no surfactant, air will
options: Flow from the larger alveolus into the smaller one
Not move, because the surface tensions are equal
Flow from the smaller alveolus into the larger one
Flow out of both alveoli equally
explanation:
Laplace's law: P = 2T/r. The smaller radius gives a higher collapsing pressure, so the small alveolus empties into the large one. Surfactant prevents this by lowering T more in small alveoli.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (Laplace law), 2018 NEET-PG (surface tension in RDS)

subject: Physiology
stem: At functional residual capacity with the glottis open and no muscle activity, which statement is correct?
options: The inward elastic recoil of the lung equals the outward recoil of the chest wall
Alveolar pressure is about −1 cm H₂O
The expiratory muscles are actively contracting
explanation:
FRC is the relaxation volume of the respiratory system. Alveolar pressure is zero (atmospheric), and intrapleural pressure is about −5 cm H₂O, reflecting the two opposing recoils.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (chest wall and lung recoil balanced at FRC), 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (FRC — 3X)
exam: 2015 AIIMS (chest wall and lung recoil balanced at FRC), 201

subject: Physiology
stem: In a patient with severe emphysema and a lot of trapped gas, which method will record the HIGHEST (truest) value of FRC?
explanation:
Plethysmography measures all gas in the thorax, including gas trapped behind closed airways. Gas-dilution methods measure only communicating gas, so they underestimate. Spirometry cannot measure FRC at all, because FRC includes the residual volume.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (FRC measurement), 2021 INI-CET (FRC raised in COPD)

subject: Physiology
stem: A spirometer contains 5 L of gas with 10% helium. A subject starts breathing from it at the end of a normal expiration. After equilibration, the helium concentration is 8%. The FRC is
explanation:
Helium is conserved: C₁V₁ = C₂(V₁ + FRC). 0.10 × 5 = 0.08 × (5 + FRC), so 0.5 = 0.4 + 0.08 FRC, and FRC = 1.25 L.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (FRC measured after normal expiration), 2015 AIIMS calculation trend
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (FRC measured after normal expiration), 2015 AI

subject: Physiology
stem: A patient has FEV₁ 2.0 L, FVC 2.4 L and a reduced total lung capacity. The pattern is
explanation:
FEV₁/FVC is 83% (normal or high) while volumes are small. In obstruction the ratio falls below 0.7, as in bronchiectasis and COPD.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (FEV₁ 1.3 / FVC 3.9), 2024 INI-CET (FEV₁/FVC < 0.7)

subject: Physiology
stem: In emphysema, which of the following is DECREASED?
explanation:
Destroyed alveolar walls reduce the surface for diffusion and the capillary bed. Loss of elastic recoil raises TLC, RV and FRC (hyperinflation).
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (parameter increased in COPD)

subject: Physiology
stem: DLCO is characteristically INCREASED in
explanation:
Extra haemoglobin inside the alveoli soaks up the CO used in the test, so DLCO rises. Polycythaemia, left-to-right shunts and asthma can also raise it. Fibrosis, anaemia and embolism lower it.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2014 AIIMS (DLCO increased in polycythaemia)

subject: Physiology
stem: Tidal volume is 500 mL, arterial PCO₂ is 40 mmHg and mixed expired PCO₂ is 28 mmHg. The physiological dead space is
explanation:
Bohr–Enghoff equation: V_D/V_T = (PaCO₂ − PECO₂)/PaCO₂ = (40 − 28)/40 = 0.3, so V_D = 0.3 × 500 = 150 mL. This matches the normal V_D/V_T of about 30%.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (normal V_D/V_T 30%), 2023 INI-CET (physiological dead space)

subject: Physiology
stem: Physiological dead space becomes much LARGER than anatomical dead space in
explanation:
Ventilated alveoli with no perfusion (V/Q → ∞) add alveolar dead space. Anatomical dead space is measured by Fowler's single-breath N₂ method; physiological dead space by the Bohr equation.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (physiological dead space — poorly perfused alveoli), 2023 NEET-PG (V/Q infinity), 2020 INI-CET (Fowler's method)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (physiological dead space — poorly perfused alv

subject: Physiology
stem: Compared with the base of an upright lung, which value is HIGHER at the apex?
explanation:
Both ventilation and perfusion are lower at the apex, but perfusion falls far more. V/Q is therefore about 3 at the apex, giving a higher PAO₂ and lower PACO₂. This is why reactivated TB favours the apex.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (V/Q approaching infinity)

subject: Physiology
stem: A drowsy patient breathing room air has PaO₂ 55 mmHg, PaCO₂ 70 mmHg and an A–a O₂ gradient of 10 mmHg. The most likely cause is
explanation:
Hypoxaemia with a normal A–a gradient means the lungs themselves are normal. The cause is either hypoventilation (here, with high CO₂) or a low inspired PO₂. V/Q mismatch, shunt and diffusion defects all widen the gradient.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (hypoxia with normal A–a gradient — hypoventilation)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (hypoxia with normal A–a gradient — hypoventila

subject: Physiology
stem: A patient at sea level breathing room air has PaCO₂ 80 mmHg (R = 0.8, PH₂O = 47 mmHg). The expected alveolar PO₂ is about
explanation:
Alveolar gas equation: PAO₂ = FiO₂(PB − PH₂O) − PaCO₂/R = 0.21 × 713 − 80/0.8 ≈ 150 − 100 = 50 mmHg.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (hypoventilation), 2015 AIIMS (PiO₂ calculation)

subject: Physiology
stem: At an altitude where barometric pressure is 380 mmHg, the PO₂ of humidified inspired air in the trachea is about
explanation:
PIO₂ = 0.21 × (380 − 47) = 0.21 × 333 ≈ 70 mmHg. Water vapour pressure stays at 47 mmHg at body temperature whatever the altitude.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (PiO₂ at altitude)

subject: Physiology
stem: All of the following are part of acclimatisation to high altitude EXCEPT
explanation:
Hypoxia stabilises HIF and raises EPO, leading to polycythaemia. Hyperventilation causes respiratory alkalosis, which the kidney compensates by losing bicarbonate. Diffuse pulmonary vasoconstriction can cause high-altitude pulmonary oedema.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (high-altitude adaptations — 3X), 2016 AIIMS (mountain climbers)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the events in a carotid body glomus cell in response to hypoxia.
1. Opening of voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels
2. Inhibition of O₂-sensitive K⁺ channels
3. Release of neurotransmitter onto afferent endings
4. Depolarisation of the glomus cell
explanation:
Hypoxia closes K⁺ channels and depolarises the cell. Ca²⁺ entry triggers release of transmitter (ATP, dopamine), which fires the carotid sinus nerve (IX) to the NTS. Peripheral chemoreceptors are most sensitive to hypoxia.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (chemoreceptors respond to hypoxia via K⁺ channels), 2023 INI-CET

subject: Physiology
stem: Central chemoreceptors on the ventral surface of the medulla are stimulated MAINLY by
options: H⁺ ions crossing directly from arterial blood
H⁺ ions formed in brain ECF from CO₂ that crosses the blood–brain barrier
explanation:
CO₂ diffuses freely into the CSF and is hydrated to H⁺ and HCO₃⁻. H⁺ itself crosses poorly, and CSF has little buffering, so CO₂ is the strongest moment-to-moment drive to breathing. Hypoxia acts only on peripheral receptors.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (peripheral chemoreceptor most sensitive to hypoxia), 2024 INI-CET (pH change and PCO₂)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (peripheral chemoreceptor most sensitive to hyp

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each respiratory centre with its function.

| Centre | Function |
|---|---|
| 1. Pre-Bötzinger complex | a. Cuts off inspiration (limits tidal volume) |
| 2. Dorsal respiratory group | b. Generates the basic respiratory rhythm |
| 3. Pneumotaxic centre | c. Prolongs inspiration (apneusis) |
| 4. Apneustic centre | d. Inspiratory neurons that integrate vagal and IX afferents |
explanation:
The ventral respiratory group is quiet in normal breathing and fires during forced expiration. The DRG lies in the nucleus tractus solitarius.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (rhythm generation — pre-Bötzinger), 2018 AIIMS (VRG in forced expiration)

subject: Physiology
stem: Which of the following shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the LEFT?
explanation:
CO raises the O₂ affinity of the remaining haem sites, which hinders unloading. Other left shifters: HbF, low 2,3-BPG, alkalosis, hypothermia. "CADET, face Right" lists the right shifters: CO₂, Acid, 2,3-DPG, Exercise, Temperature.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (right shift — not HbF), 2018 AIIMS (H⁺ lowers affinity)

subject: Physiology
stem: Blood stored for three weeks in a blood bank has
explanation:
Red cell glycolysis slows in storage, so 2,3-BPG is depleted. The curve shifts left, so transfused cells unload O₂ poorly for the first hours. 2,3-BPG normally binds the β-chains of deoxy-Hb.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (stored blood — left shift), 2023 INI-CET (2,3-BPG binds β globin)

subject: Physiology
stem: In carbon monoxide poisoning, which value remains NORMAL?
explanation:
Dissolved O₂ is unaffected, so carotid bodies are not stimulated and there is no hyperventilation. Content and true saturation fall, and P₅₀ falls (left shift). This is anaemic hypoxia.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (CO — anaemic hypoxia), 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (smoke-filled room)

subject: Physiology
stem: A patient has Hb 10 g/dL, SaO₂ 98% and PaO₂ 100 mmHg. The arterial O₂ content is about
explanation:
Content = (1.34 × Hb × SaO₂) + (0.003 × PaO₂) = (1.34 × 10 × 0.98) + 0.3 = 13.1 + 0.3 ≈ 13.4 mL/dL.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (O₂ carrying capacity with Hb 14)

subject: Physiology
stem: The Haldane effect describes the fact that
options: Acidity lowers the O₂ affinity of haemoglobin
Deoxygenated blood can carry more CO₂ than oxygenated blood
Bicarbonate leaves red cells in exchange for chloride
CO binds haemoglobin with 240 times the affinity of O₂
explanation:
Deoxy-Hb buffers H⁺ better and forms more carbamino compounds, so CO₂ is loaded in the tissues and released in the lungs. Option A is the Bohr effect; option C is the chloride (Hamburger) shift.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (H⁺ and Hb affinity — Bohr), 2023 INI-CET (2,3-BPG binding)
exam: 2018 AIIMS (H⁺ and Hb affinity — Bohr), 2023 INI-CET (2,3-BP

subject: Physiology
stem: The O₂ dissociation curve of myoglobin is hyperbolic rather than sigmoid because myoglobin
options: Has a P₅₀ higher than haemoglobin
Has a single haem with no cooperative binding
explanation:
Myoglobin's P₅₀ is about 1–2 mmHg (very high affinity), so it releases O₂ only when tissue PO₂ is very low, for example in contracting muscle.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (hyperbolic OHDC — myoglobin)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the events of the cough reflex in sequence.
1. Sudden opening of the glottis
2. Deep inspiration of about 2.5 L
3. Forceful contraction of the expiratory muscles
4. Closure of the epiglottis and vocal cords
explanation:
Pressure rises above about 100 mmHg against the closed glottis, which then opens suddenly so air rushes out. The afferents are vagal; the internal laryngeal nerve supplies the supraglottic larynx.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (mechanism of coughing)

subject: Physiology
stem: A child with cystic fibrosis has a sweat chloride of 90 mmol/L. The high sweat chloride is due to
options: Excessive Cl⁻ secretion by the secretory coil
Overactive ENaC in the sweat duct
Failure of CFTR-mediated Cl⁻ reabsorption in the sweat duct
explanation:
In the sweat duct CFTR absorbs Cl⁻, so its loss leaves salty sweat. In the airways the opposite occurs: Cl⁻ secretion fails and Na⁺ absorption increases, giving thick, dehydrated mucus.
> `RESPIRATORY SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (cystic fibrosis — chloride channel defect)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each phase of the ventricular muscle action potential with the main current.

| Phase | Current |
|---|---|
| 1. Phase 0 | a. Inward rectifier K⁺ current (I_K1) |
| 2. Phase 1 | b. L-type Ca²⁺ influx balanced by K⁺ efflux |
| 3. Phase 2 | c. Fast Na⁺ influx |
| 4. Phase 4 | d. Transient outward K⁺ current (I_to) |
explanation:
Phase 3 repolarisation is due to delayed rectifier K⁺ currents (I_Kr, I_Ks). The long plateau underlies the long refractory period.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (ventricular AP sequence — 4X)

subject: Physiology
stem: The upstroke (phase 0) of the sinoatrial node action potential is produced by
explanation:
Phase 4 slow depolarisation comes from I_f through HCN channels and then T-type Ca²⁺ channels. The slow L-type Ca²⁺ upstroke explains slow conduction in nodal tissue. Fast Na⁺ channels are inactivated at nodal potentials.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (HCN channels in rhythm generation)

subject: Physiology
stem: Vagal stimulation slows the heart rate mainly by
options: Blocking fast Na⁺ channels in the SA node
Opening ACh-activated K⁺ channels and reducing I_f
explanation:
ACh acts on M₂ receptors (Gi). The βγ subunit opens GIRK (I_K-ACh), which hyperpolarises the cell, and lower cAMP flattens the phase 4 slope. This is how a rise in BP slows the heart via the baroreflex.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (SA node influenced by ACh in response to raised BP)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (SA node influenced by ACh in response to raise

subject: Physiology
stem: Cardiac muscle cannot be tetanised because
options: Its absolute refractory period lasts almost until the end of mechanical contraction
explanation:
The long Ca²⁺ plateau keeps the cell refractory through most of systole, so a new contraction cannot add onto the one in progress. This ensures the ventricle fills.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (properties of cardiac muscle — cannot be tetanised)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (properties of cardiac muscle — cannot be tetan

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each pacemaker site with its intrinsic rate.

| Site | Intrinsic rate (per min) |
|---|---|
| 1. SA node | a. 15–40 |
| 2. AV junction | b. None (no automaticity) |
| 3. Purkinje fibres | c. 60–100 |
| 4. Ventricular myocardium | d. 40–60 |
explanation:
The fastest pacemaker controls the heart by overdrive suppression. In complete heart block, a ventricular escape rhythm of 15–40/min takes over.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (match — SAN, AVN rates, ventricular myocardium)
exam: 2018 AIIMS (match — SAN, AVN rates, ventricular myocardium)

subject: Physiology
stem: An ECG shows a constant PR interval with sudden, unpredictable dropped beats and broad QRS complexes. The block is
explanation:
Mobitz II is usually infranodal (His–Purkinje), so the QRS is often broad, and it carries a high risk of complete block. Mobitz I (progressive PR lengthening) is usually in the AV node and benign.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (progressive PR prolongation — Mobitz I, 3X)

subject: Physiology
stem: During the cardiac cycle, ventricular volume is at its LOWEST
options: At the end of isovolumetric contraction
At the end of rapid ejection
At the end of atrial systole
At the end of ejection, just before isovolumetric relaxation
explanation:
This is the end-systolic volume (about 50 mL). It stays the same through isovolumetric relaxation until the AV valves open. The c wave of the JVP occurs earlier, in isovolumetric contraction.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (c wave — isovolumetric contraction), 2020 INI-CET (ESV in exercise)

subject: Physiology
stem: Intermittent "cannon" a waves in the JVP are characteristic of
explanation:
With AV dissociation, the atrium sometimes contracts against a closed tricuspid valve. Large but regular a waves suggest tricuspid stenosis or right ventricular hypertrophy; atrial fibrillation abolishes the a wave.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (large a wave — tricuspid stenosis)

subject: Physiology
stem: The cellular basis of the Frank–Starling mechanism is
options: Better actin–myosin overlap and greater Ca²⁺ sensitivity of troponin C at longer sarcomere length
Opening of stretch-activated Na⁺ channels in the SA node
Increased heart rate with atrial stretch
explanation:
A higher end-diastolic volume stretches sarcomeres towards the optimal length (about 2.2 µm), so stroke volume rises with no change in contractility. Option D is the Bainbridge reflex.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (EDV vs force — length–tension relationship), 2014 AIIMS (preloaded muscle)

subject: Physiology
stem: The Bowditch (staircase, treppe) effect, in which contractility rises with heart rate, is explained by
options: Build-up of intracellular Ca²⁺ because there is less time to extrude it between beats
explanation:
More action potentials per minute bring in more Ca²⁺ and Na⁺. The Na⁺–K⁺ pump and NCX lag behind, so SR Ca²⁺ stores and release increase.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (Bowditch effect — 2X)

subject: Physiology
stem: During moderate dynamic exercise in a healthy person, which of the following DECREASES?
explanation:
Metabolic vasodilatation in active muscle lowers TPR, so diastolic BP changes little. Stroke volume rises (end-systolic volume falls), and cardiac output, systolic BP and pulse pressure all rise.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (ESV during exercise decreases)

subject: Physiology
stem: A subject's O₂ consumption is 250 mL/min. Arterial O₂ content is 20 mL/dL and mixed venous O₂ content is 15 mL/dL. The cardiac output is
explanation:
Fick principle: CO = VO₂ / (CaO₂ − CvO₂) = 250 mL/min ÷ 50 mL/L = 5 L/min. Remember to convert mL/dL to mL/L.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2014 AIIMS (CO from O₂ contents), 2024 INI-CET (methods of measuring CO)
exam: 2014 AIIMS (CO from O₂ contents), 2024 INI-CET (methods of m

subject: Physiology
stem: A ventricle has an end-diastolic volume of 120 mL and an end-systolic volume of 50 mL. The ejection fraction is about
explanation:
Stroke volume = 120 − 50 = 70 mL. EF = 70/120 ≈ 58%. The normal range is about 55–70%.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (cardiac index), 2020 INI-CET (ESV in exercise)

subject: Physiology
stem: If the radius of a blood vessel is halved and its length is doubled, with the pressure gradient unchanged, the flow becomes
explanation:
Poiseuille: flow ∝ r⁴/L. Halving the radius gives (1/2)⁴ = 1/16; doubling the length halves it again, giving 1/32. Radius is the strongest determinant of flow.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (diameter and length doubled — flow ×8), 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (increase vessel diameter)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (diameter and length doubled — flow ×8), 2021 I

subject: Physiology
stem: After a unilateral nephrectomy, the total peripheral resistance
options: Decreases, because there are fewer vessels
Is unchanged, because the circuits are in series
Increases, because a parallel circuit has been removed
explanation:
Organ circulations are arranged in parallel: 1/R_total = Σ 1/Rᵢ. Removing a parallel branch raises total resistance. Adding a parallel branch (for example opening muscle beds in exercise) lowers it.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (haemodynamics of flow), 2020 INI-CET (exercise)

subject: Physiology
stem: Loss of the Windkessel function of the aorta in a 75-year-old produces
options: Higher systolic, lower or unchanged diastolic pressure, and a wider pulse pressure
Lower systolic and higher diastolic pressure
Equal rises in systolic and diastolic pressure
explanation:
A stiff aorta cannot store part of the stroke volume during systole and release it in diastole. This causes isolated systolic hypertension. Elastic arteries (aorta, carotid) show the Windkessel effect; muscular arteries such as the radial do not.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (Windkessel — not radial), 2021 INI-CET (high pulse pressure in elderly)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the steps of the baroreceptor reflex after a sudden rise in carotid sinus pressure.
1. Increased firing in the glossopharyngeal (Hering's) nerve
2. Increased vagal output and reduced output from the rostral ventrolateral medulla
3. Stretch of the carotid sinus wall
4. Excitation of the nucleus tractus solitarius
explanation:
The NTS excites vagal neurons (nucleus ambiguus, dorsal motor nucleus) and, through the caudal ventrolateral medulla, inhibits the sympathetic RVLM. The result is bradycardia and vasodilatation. This is negative feedback.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (BP afferents go to NTS), 2018 AIIMS (carotid sinus — IX), 2016 AIIMS (negative feedback)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (BP afferents go to NTS), 2018 AIIMS (carotid s

subject: Physiology
stem: Blood pressure falls by 20 mmHg. The baroreceptor system brings it back up by 15 mmHg, leaving an error of 5 mmHg. The gain of the system is
explanation:
Gain = correction ÷ remaining error = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 (written −3 for negative feedback). The baroreflex has a modest gain of about 2; thermoregulation has a much higher gain of about 33.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (gain of baroreceptor system — 4)

subject: Physiology
stem: During the Valsalva manoeuvre, reflex bradycardia is seen in
explanation:
Phase I: BP rises as intrathoracic pressure is added to aortic pressure. Phase II: venous return falls, BP falls, and reflex tachycardia follows. Phase III: a brief further dip on release. Phase IV: BP overshoots into a vasoconstricted circulation, so the baroreflex slows the heart.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (rise in BP at start of Valsalva)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (rise in BP at start of Valsalva)

subject: Physiology
stem: A patient with an acute inferior wall MI develops sudden bradycardia, hypotension and slow breathing. This reflex arises from
options: Chemosensitive vagal C-fibre endings in the left ventricle (Bezold–Jarisch reflex)
A raised intracranial pressure response (Cushing reflex)
explanation:
These receptors, concentrated in the inferoposterior wall, are activated by ischaemia, serotonin and veratridine. They produce the triad of bradycardia, hypotension and apnoea or hypopnoea.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (Bezold–Jarisch triad), 2015 AIIMS (serotonin as mediator)

subject: Physiology
stem: A rapid intravenous infusion of saline raises the heart rate even though blood pressure rises slightly. This is because of
options: The Bainbridge reflex, triggered by atrial stretch
explanation:
Stretch receptors at the veno-atrial junctions send vagal afferents that raise sympathetic drive to the SA node. Direct stretch of the SA node also contributes.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (atrial volume and heart rate), 2021 NEET-PG (Bainbridge reflex)
exam: 2016 AIIMS (atrial volume and heart rate), 2021 NEET-PG (Bai

subject: Physiology
stem: At rest, which organ has the HIGHEST arteriovenous O₂ difference?
explanation:
The myocardium extracts about 70–75% of delivered O₂ even at rest. More O₂ therefore has to come from more coronary flow. The kidney has one of the lowest A–V differences, because its high flow exceeds its metabolic needs.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (least A–V difference — kidney)

subject: Physiology
stem: After a 1-litre haemorrhage, which hormone level FALLS?
explanation:
Reduced atrial stretch (low CVP) cuts ANP secretion. Reduced baroreceptor and volume receptor firing raises ADH, renin–angiotensin II–aldosterone and thirst.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (decrease in CVP — ↑ADH, AngII, thirst, ↓ANP)

subject: Physiology
stem: In a capillary, hydrostatic pressure is 30 mmHg, interstitial hydrostatic pressure is −3 mmHg, plasma oncotic pressure is 28 mmHg and interstitial oncotic pressure is 8 mmHg. The net filtration pressure is
explanation:
NFP = (Pc − Pi) − (πc − πi) = (30 − (−3)) − (28 − 8) = 33 − 20 = +13 mmHg. A positive value favours filtration.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (net filtration pressure calculation), Starling forces

subject: Physiology
stem: Catecholamines speed myocardial relaxation (positive lusitropy) mainly by phosphorylating
explanation:
β₁ → cAMP → PKA phosphorylates phospholamban, which releases its brake on SERCA2a, so Ca²⁺ is pumped back into the SR faster. PKA also phosphorylates troponin I, lowering its Ca²⁺ sensitivity.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (lusitropy enhanced by catecholamines)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each hormone with its receptor signalling mechanism.

| Hormone | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Insulin | a. Receptor guanylyl cyclase (cGMP) |
| 2. Growth hormone | b. Gq — IP₃/DAG — Ca²⁺ |
| 3. Atrial natriuretic peptide | c. Receptor tyrosine kinase |
| 4. TRH | d. JAK–STAT (cytokine receptor) |
explanation:
Prolactin, leptin, EPO and the cytokines also use JAK–STAT. Nitric oxide uses soluble guanylyl cyclase, whereas ANP and BNP use membrane-bound guanylyl cyclase.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (match — insulin, GH, ACh, T), 2021 INI-CET (leptin — JAK–STAT)

subject: Physiology
stem: For which hormone is the receptor located in the nucleus and bound to DNA even when no hormone is present?
explanation:
The thyroid hormone receptor (with RXR) sits on thyroid response elements. Hormone binding swaps co-repressors for co-activators. Glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid receptors sit in the cytoplasm bound to heat-shock proteins and move to the nucleus after binding hormone.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (hormone with nuclear receptor — thyroxine), 2020 INI-CET (hormone crossing plasma membrane)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the steps of glucagon signalling in a hepatocyte.
1. Activation of protein kinase A
2. Activation of the Gs α subunit
3. Glucagon binding to its G-protein-coupled receptor
4. Activation of adenylyl cyclase and a rise in cAMP
explanation:
Gs exchanges GDP for GTP, its α subunit activates adenylyl cyclase, and cAMP activates PKA. PKA then phosphorylates enzymes of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. β₂ receptors use the same pathway.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (sequence — adenylyl cyclase → cAMP → PKA), 2022 NEET-PG (β₂ via adenylate cyclase)

subject: Physiology
stem: After the pituitary stalk is cut in a road traffic accident, which anterior pituitary hormone RISES?
explanation:
Prolactin is under mainly tonic inhibitory control by hypothalamic dopamine. Cutting the stalk removes that inhibition, while the hormones that depend on stimulatory releasing hormones fall.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (hormones under inhibitory hypothalamic control — GH, prolactin)

subject: Physiology
stem: Growth hormone secretion is increased by all of the following EXCEPT
explanation:
A glucose load suppresses GH; failure to suppress during an oral glucose tolerance test confirms acromegaly. Fasting, arginine, ghrelin and stress all raise GH.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (hormone elevated in exercise and sleep — GH), 2022 INI-CET (acromegaly)

subject: Physiology
stem: Which action of growth hormone is DIRECT and not mediated by IGF-1?
options: Proliferation of chondrocytes in the growth plate
Increased lipolysis and a rise in blood glucose
explanation:
GH's metabolic, anti-insulin actions are direct. Its growth-promoting actions are largely through IGF-1, which is made mainly in the liver and is structurally similar to proinsulin and insulin.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (IGF-1 mainly from liver), 2024 INI-CET (IGF similar to insulin)
exam: 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (IGF-1 mainly from liver), 2024 IN

subject: Physiology
stem: The major hormonal regulator of fetal growth is
explanation:
Fetal growth depends on insulin, IGF-2 (and IGF-1) and nutrient supply. Fetal GH receptors are scarce, so babies lacking GH have near-normal birth length.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (hormone with no significant role in in-utero growth — GH)

subject: Physiology
stem: Leptin reduces food intake by acting on the arcuate nucleus to
options: Stimulate POMC (α-MSH) neurons and inhibit NPY/AgRP neurons
explanation:
α-MSH acting on MC4 receptors produces satiety. Leptin also signals energy sufficiency and has a permissive role in the onset of puberty (via kisspeptin/GnRH).
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (leptin permissive for puberty — 3X), 2021 INI-CET (leptin — JAK–STAT)

subject: Physiology
stem: ADH increases the permeability to urea of the
explanation:
Through V₂ receptors and cAMP, ADH inserts aquaporin-2 into the principal cells. In the inner medulla it also activates urea transporters UT-A1/A3, which feeds urea recycling and helps build the medullary gradient.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (mechanism of ADH — water and urea), 2018 AIIMS (aquaporin-2)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (mechanism of ADH — water and urea), 2018 AIIMS

subject: Physiology
stem: In SIADH, urine flow eventually increases despite persistently high ADH ("vasopressin escape"). This is mainly because of
options: Downregulation of aquaporin-2 expression in the collecting duct
explanation:
Volume expansion also causes natriuresis (ANP, pressure natriuresis). Together these limit water retention, which is why SIADH patients are euvolaemic without oedema.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (vasopressin escape — 2X)

subject: Physiology
stem: In a water deprivation test, urine osmolality stays below 300 mOsm/kg and does not rise after desmopressin. The diagnosis is
explanation:
The collecting duct cannot respond (V₂ receptor or aquaporin-2 defect, or lithium). In central DI, urine concentrates after desmopressin. In primary polydipsia, urine concentrates with dehydration alone.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (impaired aquaporin — nephrogenic DI)

subject: Physiology
stem: The zona glomerulosa cannot synthesise cortisol because it lacks
explanation:
Without 17α-hydroxylation, pregnenolone can only go down the mineralocorticoid pathway. Aldosterone synthase is expressed only in the glomerulosa, so only that zone can make aldosterone.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (match — zones and hormones), 2022 INI-CET (zona glomerulosa — electrolyte balance), 2015 AIIMS (pregnenolone)

subject: Physiology
stem: Months after bilateral adrenalectomy, a patient develops progressive skin darkening. The pigmentation is due to
options: Increased POMC-derived ACTH and MSH acting on melanocortin-1 receptors
explanation:
Loss of cortisol feedback drives POMC processing. ACTH shares its MSH sequence and stimulates melanocytes (Nelson's syndrome when a corticotroph tumour enlarges).
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (adrenalectomy — pigmentation and fatigue)

subject: Physiology
stem: All of the following stimulate catecholamine secretion from the adrenal medulla EXCEPT
explanation:
Medullary secretion is driven by preganglionic sympathetic (ACh, nicotinic) discharge during stress: exercise, standing up, hypoglycaemia, haemorrhage, cold and smoking. About 80% of the output is epinephrine.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (adrenal medulla secretes in response to … not hyperglycaemia)

stem: An asthmatic develops hypokalaemia after repeated salbutamol nebulisation. The mechanism is
options: β₂-mediated stimulation of Na⁺–K⁺ ATPase, shifting K⁺ into cells
Increased renal K⁺ secretion caused by aldosterone
explanation:
The same shift explains the low K⁺ after epinephrine release during stress. Insulin also drives K⁺ into cells, which is why insulin with glucose is used to treat hyperkalaemia.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (ECF K⁺ decreased by epinephrine), 2017 AIIMS (insulin and K⁺ — T/F)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each glucose transporter with its main site and feature.

| Transporter | Site and feature |
|---|---|
| 1. GLUT1 | a. Skeletal muscle and adipose tissue — insulin-dependent |
| 2. GLUT2 | b. RBCs and blood–brain barrier — basal uptake |
| 3. GLUT4 | c. Enterocyte apical membrane — fructose |
| 4. GLUT5 | d. β-cells and hepatocytes — low affinity, glucose sensor |
explanation:
Insulin moves GLUT4 from vesicles to the membrane, so insulin-dependent glucose uptake occurs in adipose tissue and muscle. Exercise also recruits GLUT4 without insulin, which improves insulin resistance.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (insulin-dependent glucose transport), 2023 NEET-PG (GLUT4 and insulin resistance)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the steps of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from a β-cell.
1. Closure of ATP-sensitive K⁺ channels
2. Glucose entry through GLUT2 and glycolysis, raising ATP
3. Ca²⁺ influx through voltage-gated channels and exocytosis
4. Depolarisation of the β-cell membrane
explanation:
Sulfonylureas act by closing the K_ATP channel (SUR1 subunit); diazoxide opens it. Insulin and C-peptide are released in equal (equimolar) amounts.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (C-peptide in proinsulin), 2023 INI-CET (insulin)

subject: Physiology
stem: A non-diabetic nurse has recurrent hypoglycaemia with very high serum insulin but a suppressed C-peptide. The most likely cause is
explanation:
C-peptide is cleaved from proinsulin and released with endogenous insulin. Commercial insulin contains none, so C-peptide is suppressed. Insulinoma and sulfonylureas raise both insulin and C-peptide.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (C-peptide in proinsulin)

subject: Physiology
stem: Most of the circulating T₃ is produced by
explanation:
About 80% of T₃ comes from T₄ in liver, kidney and muscle (deiodinases D1 and D2). T₄ binds TBG with higher affinity than T₃, so T₄ has the longer half-life.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (T₄ has greater affinity for TBG), 2020 INI-CET (thyroxine crosses membrane)

subject: Physiology
stem: Iodide is transported from the thyroid follicular cell into the colloid by
options: Na⁺–I⁻ symporter on the basolateral membrane
explanation:
The Na⁺–I⁻ symporter (NIS) traps iodide at the basolateral side. Pendrin (a Cl⁻/I⁻ exchanger) moves it into the colloid, where TPO oxidises and organifies it. Pendred syndrome is goitre with sensorineural deafness.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (iodine transport — sodium–iodide symporter)

subject: Physiology
stem: Parathyroid hormone increases urinary phosphate excretion by
options: Inhibiting NaPi-IIa cotransporters in the proximal tubule
Stimulating phosphate secretion in the collecting duct
Inhibiting TRPV5 in the distal tubule
explanation:
PTH also increases Ca²⁺ reabsorption in the distal tubule (TRPV5, the opposite of option D), stimulates renal 1α-hydroxylase, and raises bone resorption via RANKL on osteoblasts, which activates osteoclasts.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (PTH raises Ca — 3X)

subject: Physiology
stem: Inhibin, secreted by Sertoli cells, selectively inhibits the secretion of
explanation:
FSH acts on Sertoli cells (ABP, inhibin); LH acts on Leydig cells (testosterone). Testosterone feeds back mainly on LH and GnRH. SHBG binds testosterone more tightly than oestradiol.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (testosterone — Leydig cells), 2015 AIIMS (SHBG — testosterone)

subject: Physiology
stem: Although prolactin rises throughout pregnancy, milk secretion does not begin until after delivery because
options: Prolactin receptors appear only after birth
High oestrogen and progesterone block prolactin's action on the breast
Dopamine levels are high in pregnancy
explanation:
When the placenta is delivered, steroid levels fall abruptly and lactogenesis starts. Prolactin peaks in late pregnancy and the first postpartum week.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (prolactin high 1 week after delivery)

subject: Physiology
stem: A woman with rapidly progressive hirsutism has a markedly raised DHEA-S with normal testosterone. The most likely source of the androgen is the
explanation:
In women, DHEA-S comes almost entirely from the adrenal, which makes it a marker of adrenal androgen excess (tumour or CAH). A disproportionate rise in testosterone points to the ovary.
> `ENDOCRINE SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (hormone exclusively secreted by adrenal in females — DHEA-S)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each cutaneous receptor with its principal function.

| Receptor | Function |
|---|---|
| 1. Meissner corpuscle | a. Skin stretch; slowly adapting |
| 2. Merkel disc | b. High-frequency vibration; rapidly adapting |
| 3. Pacinian corpuscle | c. Static touch and two-point discrimination; slowly adapting |
| 4. Ruffini ending | d. Flutter and light moving touch; rapidly adapting |
explanation:
Pacinian corpuscles respond best at about 200–300 Hz and Meissner corpuscles at about 30–50 Hz. Merkel discs give the sustained, fine spatial detail used in reading Braille.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (static two-point — Merkel), 2022 NEET-PG (fast vibration — Pacinian), 2021 INI-CET (Meissner, Pacinian)

subject: Physiology
stem: When excessive tension develops in a contracting muscle, the muscle suddenly relaxes. The receptor and pathway responsible are
options: Muscle spindle — Ia afferents exciting the agonist
Golgi tendon organ — Ib afferents producing autogenic inhibition
explanation:
GTOs lie in series with the muscle fibres and signal tension. Through inhibitory interneurons they relax the same muscle. Spindles lie in parallel and signal length.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2015 AIIMS (GTO responds to tension — 4X)

subject: Physiology
stem: During a voluntary contraction, γ motor neurons fire together with α motor neurons. The purpose of this α–γ co-activation is to
options: Directly increase the force of contraction
Keep the muscle spindle sensitive while the muscle shortens
Produce reciprocal inhibition of the antagonist
explanation:
γ (Aγ) efferents contract the intrafusal fibres, so the spindle does not go slack and keeps reporting length. Increased γ drive also explains the Jendrassik manoeuvre and decerebrate rigidity.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (spindle supplied by Aγ fibres)

subject: Physiology
stem: According to the Weber–Fechner law, the perceived intensity of a sensation is proportional to
options: The logarithm of the stimulus intensity
The square of the stimulus intensity
The stimulus intensity in a linear way
explanation:
A just-noticeable difference is a constant fraction of the baseline (ΔI/I = constant). Stevens' power law is the modern alternative. *The 2022 INI-CET key's "directly proportional to intensity" is an oversimplification.*
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (Weber–Fechner — 3X)

subject: Physiology
stem: Rubbing a bruised shin relieves the pain because large Aβ fibres activate inhibitory interneurons located in
options: The substantia gelatinosa (lamina II) of the dorsal horn
explanation:
This is Melzack and Wall's gate control theory, which is also the basis of TENS. The PAG works through descending pathways, not the segmental gate.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (massage — substantia gelatinosa), 2021 INI-CET (TENS — gate control), 2020 INI-CET (PAG)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the descending pain-inhibitory pathway in sequence.
1. Nucleus raphe magnus (serotonergic) in the rostral ventromedial medulla
2. Enkephalin-releasing interneurons in the dorsal horn
3. Periaqueductal grey of the midbrain
4. Reduced substance P release from primary nociceptive afferents
explanation:
The opioid-sensitive PAG drives the raphe nuclei, whose fibres descend in the dorsolateral funiculus. Enkephalin then acts presynaptically on C and Aδ terminals and postsynaptically on dorsal horn neurons.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (PAG relieves pain), 2021 INI-CET (gate control)

subject: Physiology
stem: A patient with sunburn finds that the light touch of a cotton shirt is painful. This phenomenon is
explanation:
Allodynia is pain from a stimulus that is normally painless. Hyperalgesia is an exaggerated response to a stimulus that is normally painful. Both result from inflammatory sensitisation (carrageenan is used experimentally to induce inflammatory pain).
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (sunburn and lukewarm water — allodynia), 2024 INI-CET (carrageenan — inflammatory pain)

subject: Physiology
stem: Which nerve fibres are MOST susceptible to hypoxia?
explanation:
Ganong's order of susceptibility: hypoxia B > A > C; pressure A > B > C (so pressure palsies hit touch and motor first); local anaesthetic C > B > A.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (Saturday night palsy — type A), 2017 AIIMS (fibres and local anaesthetic)

subject: Physiology
stem: During the "chill" phase at the onset of fever, the patient shivers and has cold peripheries because
options: The hypothalamic set point has risen above the current core temperature
explanation:
Pyrogens (IL-1, IL-6, TNF) induce PGE₂, which acts on the preoptic area and raises the set point. The body then conserves and produces heat until core temperature reaches the new set point. When the fever breaks ("crisis"), sweating and vasodilatation follow.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (preoptic nucleus in fever), 2021 NEET-PG (raised set point — shivering)

subject: Physiology
stem: The feature that best distinguishes heat stroke from heat exhaustion is
options: Core temperature above 40°C with CNS dysfunction, often with hot, dry skin
explanation:
In classic heat stroke, thermoregulation fails and sweating stops. In heat exhaustion, sweating continues, mentation is preserved, and the problem is mainly salt and water depletion.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (heat stroke — sweating not seen, 4X)
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (heat stroke — sweating not seen

subject: Physiology
stem:
Match each EEG pattern with its state.

| EEG pattern | State |
|---|---|
| 1. Alpha rhythm (8–13 Hz) | a. Stage N3 (deep sleep) |
| 2. Sleep spindles and K complexes | b. REM sleep |
| 3. High-amplitude delta waves | c. Awake, relaxed, eyes closed |
| 4. Low-voltage, fast "sawtooth" waves | d. Stage N2 |
explanation:
Alpha waves are blocked by opening the eyes (alpha block). Stage N2 takes up about half of total sleep time.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (K complexes — N2), 2020 INI-CET (alpha reduced on eye opening)

subject: Physiology
stem: Which feature is characteristic of REM sleep?
options: Atonia of skeletal muscles except the extraocular muscles and diaphragm
Lowest cerebral O₂ consumption of the night
explanation:
REM sleep has vivid dreams, irregular heart rate and breathing, penile tumescence and raised brain metabolism. Sleepwalking and night terrors arise from N3. Polysomnography records EEG, EOG, EMG and oximetry.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (EEG sleep stages), 2016 AIIMS (polysomnography)

subject: Physiology
stem: "Sleep pressure" that builds up during prolonged wakefulness is mainly due to the accumulation of
explanation:
Adenosine from ATP breakdown builds up and acts on A₁/A₂A receptors to promote sleep. Caffeine blocks these receptors and promotes wakefulness. Orexin and histamine are wake-promoting.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (caffeine blocks adenosine)

subject: Physiology
stem: The output of the cerebellar cortex is carried by Purkinje cells, which are
options: Inhibitory (GABA) to the deep cerebellar and vestibular nuclei
Inhibitory directly to the motor cortex
explanation:
Purkinje cells are the sole output of the cortex. They receive climbing fibres from the inferior olive and mossy fibres via granule cells. Excitatory signals leave the cerebellum only from the deep nuclei.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (Purkinje projects to deep nuclei; inferior olive fibres), 2019 NEET-PG (Purkinje cells)
exam: 2020 INI-CET (Purkinje projects to deep nuclei; inferior oli

subject: Physiology
stem: In Parkinson's disease, loss of nigrostriatal dopamine leads to
options: Decreased GPi output and disinhibition of the thalamus
Increased GPi/SNr output, causing excessive inhibition of the thalamus
Increased activity of the direct pathway
explanation:
Dopamine excites the direct pathway (D₁) and inhibits the indirect pathway (D₂). Losing it shifts the balance towards the indirect pathway, producing hypokinesia. Lesions of the subthalamic nucleus do the opposite, giving hemiballismus.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (hemiballismus — subthalamic nucleus)

subject: Physiology
stem: Which finding indicates an upper motor neuron lesion rather than a lower motor neuron lesion?
options: Clasp-knife spasticity with an extensor plantar response
explanation:
UMN lesions cause spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus and a Babinski sign, with only disuse wasting. LMN lesions cause flaccidity, early atrophy, fasciculations and areflexia.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (LMN lesion features)

subject: Physiology
stem: Decerebrate rigidity in an experimental animal (transection between the colliculi) is abolished by
options: Cutting the dorsal roots of the affected limbs
explanation:
Decerebrate rigidity is "γ rigidity": the vestibulospinal and reticulospinal pathways are released from inhibition and increase γ drive, which works through the spindle (Ia) loop. Decorticate rigidity is less severe because the red nucleus pathway is preserved.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (decorticate less than decerebrate), 2018 AIIMS (decorticate rigidity)

subject: Physiology
stem:
Arrange the steps of phototransduction in a rod when light falls on it.
1. Closure of cGMP-gated Na⁺ channels and hyperpolarisation
2. Isomerisation of 11-cis-retinal to all-trans-retinal
3. Activation of phosphodiesterase, which hydrolyses cGMP
4. Activation of transducin (Gt)
explanation:
Rhodopsin sits in the discs of the outer segment. In darkness, cGMP keeps Na⁺ channels open (the "dark current"), so the rod is depolarised and releases glutamate continuously. Light reduces that release.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (discs in outer segment of photoreceptor)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (discs in outer segment of photoreceptor)

subject: Physiology
stem: The endocochlear potential of about +80 mV is generated by
explanation:
The stria secretes K⁺ into the endolymph. The large driving force for K⁺ entry through hair-cell transduction channels makes the cochlea very sensitive. Loop diuretics can reduce this potential (ototoxicity).
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2014 AIIMS (endocochlear potential +85 mV)

subject: Physiology
stem: About 95% of the afferent fibres of the spiral ganglion synapse on the
explanation:
Inner hair cells are the true sensory receptors. Outer hair cells receive mainly efferent fibres and act as the "cochlear amplifier" through the motor protein prestin; they are the source of otoacoustic emissions.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (spiral ganglion processes end at inner hair cells)
