subject: Microbiology
stem: Ventilator-associated pneumonia grows a non-motile, oxidase-negative Gram-negative coccobacillus that is resistant to carbapenems. The most likely organism and a last-resort drug are
explanation:
Acinetobacter survives for long periods on dry hospital surfaces and develops resistance quickly. Colistin is nephrotoxic and neurotoxic.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (VAP — Acinetobacter), 2016 AIIMS pharm (Acinetobacter VAP — colistin)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A smoker has atypical pneumonia with diarrhoea, confusion and hyponatraemia after an outbreak traced to a cooling tower. The fastest diagnostic test is
explanation:
Legionella grows on BCYE agar (with cysteine and iron) and stains poorly with Gram stain. It is an intracellular organism of macrophages, so macrolides or fluoroquinolones are used.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (culture medium for Legionella — BCYE)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A child admitted with whooping cough should be placed under
options: Airborne precautions in a negative-pressure room
explanation:
Particles larger than 5 µm travel about 1 metre (pertussis, meningococcus, influenza, diphtheria). Airborne isolation is for droplet nuclei (TB, measles, varicella). Contact isolation is for MRSA, *C. difficile* and VRE.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (droplet isolation — pertussis), 2018 AIIMS (contact isolation — MRSA), 2014 AIIMS (droplet nuclei — T/F)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Four weeks after treatment to eradicate H. pylori, the test of choice to confirm cure is
options: Urea breath test (or stool antigen), done off PPIs
Rapid urease test on any biopsy, even during PPI use
explanation:
Antibodies stay positive for months after eradication. PPIs suppress urease and cause false negatives, so they are stopped for 2 weeks before testing.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (urea breath test — H. pylori)
exam: 2023 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (urea breath test — H. pylori)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Ascending flaccid paralysis two weeks after bloody diarrhoea is most often linked to infection with
options: Campylobacter jejuni, through molecular mimicry with nerve gangliosides
explanation:
Campylobacter grows at 42 °C in microaerophilic conditions (Skirrow medium) and has a comma or "seagull" shape. It is a leading cause of bacterial enteritis worldwide.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (Campylobacter — 42 °C, microaerophilic)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The infectious, metabolically inactive, extracellular form of Chlamydia trachomatis is the
explanation:
The elementary body enters cells and becomes the dividing reticulate body inside an inclusion. Neonatal chlamydial conjunctivitis appears at 5–14 days. An afebrile "staccato cough" pneumonia with eosinophilia follows at 4–12 weeks and is treated with oral erythromycin or azithromycin.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonitis — C. trachomatis)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonitis — C. t

subject: Microbiology
stem: A woman has a thin grey, fishy-smelling vaginal discharge. All of the following support bacterial vaginosis EXCEPT
options: A positive whiff test with KOH
explanation:
In bacterial vaginosis, lactobacilli are replaced by Gardnerella and anaerobes with little inflammation (Amsel criteria, Nugent score). Pseudohyphae point to candidiasis, which has a normal pH.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (epithelial cells studded with bacteria — Gardnerella)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (epithelial cells studded with bacteria — Gardn

subject: Microbiology
stem: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is intrinsically resistant to β-lactams because it
options: Lacks a peptidoglycan cell wall (sterols in its membrane)
explanation:
Mycoplasma forms "fried-egg" colonies, causes atypical pneumonia, and induces cold agglutinins (anti-I IgM). Ureaplasma is a urease-positive mollicute linked to urethritis and preterm birth.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (mollicute — Ureaplasma), 2017 AIIMS pharm (Mycoplasma resistant to β-lactams)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The repeated febrile relapses of louse-borne relapsing fever are caused by
options: Antigenic variation of variable major outer-membrane proteins
explanation:
*Borrelia recurrentis* is seen in blood films taken during fever. Each new antigenic variant escapes existing antibody. *B. vincentii* with fusobacteria causes Vincent's angina.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (relapsing fever and Vincent's angina — Borrelia)
exam: 2017 AIIMS (relapsing fever and Vincent's angina — Borrelia)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A Giemsa-stained aspirate from a tender bubo shows bipolar ("safety-pin") Gram-negative bacilli. The disease is transmitted to humans by the
explanation:
The organism is *Yersinia pestis*. Blockage of the flea's gut makes it regurgitate bacilli while feeding. Bubonic plague may progress to septicaemic or pneumonic forms, the latter spreading person to person by droplets.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (rat reservoir, blackish limbs — Xenopsylla)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A trekker develops a tender ulcer with an eschar and regional lymphadenopathy after skinning a wild rabbit. The organism is
explanation:
Ulceroglandular tularaemia follows contact with infected animals or a tick bite. Diagnosis is serological, since culture is hazardous for laboratory staff and needs BSL-3. *Pasteurella* follows cat and dog bites.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (category A agents), 2022 INI-CET (BSL-3)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A child has a painless, non-tender regional lymphadenopathy 2 weeks after being scratched by a kitten. Node biopsy shows stellate granulomas with central neutrophils. The organism is best shown by
explanation:
*Bartonella henselae* causes cat-scratch disease. In immunocompromised patients the same organism causes bacillary angiomatosis. *B. bacilliformis* causes Oroya fever.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2016 AIIMS (stellate granuloma — cat scratch), 2023 INI-CET (match — Oroya fever)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each selective or special medium with the organism it is used for.

| Medium | Organism |
|---|---|
| 1. Thayer–Martin (VCN) | a. Corynebacterium diphtheriae |
| 2. Potassium tellurite | b. Legionella pneumophila |
| 3. Buffered charcoal yeast extract | c. Neisseria gonorrhoeae |
| 4. Lowenstein–Jensen | d. Mycobacterium tuberculosis |
explanation:
Selective media contain inhibitors (antibiotics, tellurite, dyes) that suppress normal flora. EMJH is used for leptospira and Skirrow medium for campylobacter.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (Thayer–Martin), 2022 NEET-PG (BCYE), 2023 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (EMJH)

subject: Microbiology
stem: CLED medium is preferred to MacConkey agar for urine culture because it
options: Is selective for Gram-negative bacilli only
Prevents swarming of Proteus and also supports Gram-positive cocci and yeasts
explanation:
Cystine Lactose Electrolyte Deficient medium is electrolyte-deficient, which stops *Proteus* swarming, and is non-selective, so enterococci, staphylococci and candida all grow and can be counted.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2014 AIIMS (CLED better than MacConkey), 2015 AIIMS (swarming — Proteus)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A man who cleans fish tanks develops nodules spreading up the forearm along lymphatics. Biopsy culture is positive at 30 °C but not 37 °C. The organism is
explanation:
"Fish-tank granuloma" grows best at 30–33 °C, which is why it stays in cool skin. Nodular lymphangitis (sporotrichoid spread) is also caused by *Sporothrix*, *Nocardia brasiliensis* and *Leishmania*.
> `BACTERIOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (nodules along lymphatics — Sporothrix, Nocardia, M. marinum)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each hepatitis virus with its genome and route of spread.

| Virus | Genome and route |
|---|---|
| 1. Hepatitis A | a. Partially double-stranded DNA; parenteral and sexual |
| 2. Hepatitis B | b. Single-stranded RNA; faecal–oral; severe in pregnancy |
| 3. Hepatitis C | c. Single-stranded RNA, picornavirus; faecal–oral |
| 4. Hepatitis E | d. Single-stranded RNA, flavivirus; parenteral; often chronic |
explanation:
Hepatitis A and E are water-borne and never become chronic. Hepatitis E carries a high mortality (about 20%) in the third trimester of pregnancy. Hepatitis B and C are the two that cause chronic infection and hepatocellular carcinoma.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (water-borne hepatitis), 2014 AIIMS (reverse transcriptase — HIV and HBV)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A health worker's serology shows HBsAg negative, anti-HBs positive, total anti-HBc negative. This pattern means
explanation:
The vaccine contains only HBsAg, so it produces anti-HBs without anti-HBc. Past infection gives anti-HBs **and** anti-HBc. Isolated total anti-HBc with nothing else suggests past infection with waned anti-HBs, as in the 2021 question.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (serology — past infection, 2X), 2021 INI-CET (subunit vaccine — HBsAg), 2018 NEET-PG (HBsAg + IgM anti-HBc — acute)

subject: Microbiology
stem: HBeAg positivity in a chronic hepatitis B carrier indicates
options: Active viral replication and high infectivity
explanation:
HBeAg correlates with high HBV DNA. Mothers who are HBeAg positive have a much higher risk of transmitting infection perinatally, which is why newborns receive vaccine plus hepatitis B immunoglobulin within 12 hours.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (hepatitis serology), 2018 AIIMS (eye splash risk), 2018 AIIMS (HBV and HCV — inform spouse)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The confirmatory test for active hepatitis C infection after a positive antibody screen is
options: HCV RNA by nucleic acid amplification
explanation:
Antibody persists after spontaneous or treated clearance, so it cannot distinguish past from present infection. NAAT also confirms cure (sustained virological response) 12 weeks after direct-acting antivirals.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (NAAT for HCV — T/F)

subject: Microbiology
stem: An infant born to an HIV-positive mother is 4 months old. The appropriate test to establish whether the baby is infected is
options: HIV DNA PCR on dried blood spot
explanation:
Maternal IgG crosses the placenta and persists up to 18 months, so antibody tests cannot be interpreted before then. Virological tests (DNA or RNA PCR) are used at 6 weeks and repeated later.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG (4-month-old of HIV mother — dried blood for PCR)
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (4-month-old of HIV mother — dried blood for PC

subject: Microbiology
stem: In a person on antiretroviral therapy, the single best marker of treatment success is
explanation:
Viral load responds within weeks, while CD4 recovery is slower and more variable. "Undetectable equals untransmittable" is based on sustained viral suppression. High maternal viral load is the strongest predictor of vertical transmission.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG (HAART monitored by viral load), 2018 AIIMS (vertical transmission — high RNA load)
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (HAART monitored by viral load), 2018 AIIMS (ve

subject: Microbiology
stem: The HIV envelope glycoprotein that mediates fusion of the viral envelope with the host cell membrane is
explanation:
gp120 binds CD4 and the co-receptor (CCR5 or CXCR4); gp41 then inserts its fusion peptide into the cell membrane. Enfuvirtide blocks gp41, and maraviroc blocks CCR5. p24 is the capsid antigen used in fourth-generation tests.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (structure permeating host membrane — gp41)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A 4-day-old neonate has vesicles, seizures and CSF showing lymphocytes with a normal glucose. The mother had painful genital ulcers near delivery. The best confirmatory test is
explanation:
PCR is sensitive, specific and fast. A Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells but does not separate HSV from VZV or confirm CNS disease. Neonatal HSV is usually HSV-2 acquired during delivery, and acyclovir is started empirically.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (HSV encephalitis — CSF PCR), 2023 INI-CET (neonate with CNS signs — HSV-2), 2024 INI-CET (genital vesicles — acyclovir)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Herpes simplex virus establishes latency in
options: Dorsal root and trigeminal sensory ganglia
explanation:
VZV also stays latent in sensory ganglia and reactivates as shingles in one dermatome. EBV remains latent in B cells (through CD21), and CMV in monocytes and marrow progenitors.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (herpes latency — dorsal root ganglion), 2021 NEET-PG (dermatomal vesicles — zoster), 2020 INI-CET (EBV receptor CD21)
exam: 2017 AIIMS (herpes latency — dorsal root ganglion), 2021 NEE

subject: Microbiology
stem: A woman at 14 weeks of pregnancy is exposed to a child with chickenpox. She has no history of varicella, and VZV IgG is negative. The correct action is
options: Give varicella-zoster immunoglobulin as soon as possible
explanation:
She is susceptible. The live attenuated vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy. Varicella in the first 20 weeks can cause congenital varicella syndrome (limb hypoplasia, cicatricial scars, eye defects).
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (pregnant, VZV antibody negative — susceptible)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A renal transplant recipient develops fever, leucopenia and pneumonitis 2 months after transplantation. Biopsy shows large cells with intranuclear "owl-eye" inclusions. Treatment is
explanation:
CMV is the commonest cause of infection 1–4 months after transplantation. Monitoring is by quantitative CMV DNA PCR. Foscarnet is used for ganciclovir-resistant strains; it needs no activation by viral kinase.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG / 2020 NEET-PG (CMV 1–4 months post-transplant), 2022 NEET-PG (owl-eye in urine), 2021 INI-CET (foscarnet — no thymidine kinase activation)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The preferred specimen to confirm congenital CMV infection in a newborn within the first 3 weeks of life is
explanation:
CMV is shed in large amounts in urine and saliva. Testing must be done before 3 weeks of age; after that, a positive result cannot distinguish congenital from perinatal infection. Congenital CMV causes periventricular calcification and sensorineural deafness.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (best sample for CMV DNA PCR in neonate — urine)
exam: 2016 AIIMS (best sample for CMV DNA PCR in neonate — urine)

subject: Microbiology
stem: An adolescent has fever, sore throat, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and atypical lymphocytes. The monospot test detects
options: Specific IgM against viral capsid antigen
Heterophile antibodies that agglutinate horse or sheep red cells
explanation:
This is the principle of the Paul–Bunnell test. It is often negative in young children and early in illness, when EBV-specific VCA IgM is used instead. Giving ampicillin produces a florid rash.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (Paul–Bunnell — heterophile antibody, 2X), 2014 AIIMS (EBV and nasopharyngeal carcinoma)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Oral hairy leukoplakia in a person with HIV presents as white plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off. It is caused by
explanation:
The key distinction is that oral candidiasis (pseudomembranous thrush) **can** be wiped off, leaving a raw surface. EBV is also linked to Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (white patches that cannot be wiped — EBV), 2024 INI-CET (odynophagia with plaques — candida)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (white patches that cannot be wiped — EBV), 202

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each virus with the tumour it is associated with.

| Virus | Tumour |
|---|---|
| 1. HHV-8 | a. Cervical carcinoma |
| 2. HPV 16 and 18 | b. Adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma |
| 3. HTLV-1 | c. Hepatocellular carcinoma |
| 4. Hepatitis B | d. Kaposi sarcoma |
explanation:
HHV-8 also causes primary effusion lymphoma and multicentric Castleman disease. HPV 6 and 11 are low-risk types causing genital warts, and the nonavalent vaccine covers 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52 and 58.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (HHV-8), 2024 INI-CET (HPV 16, 18), 2019 NEET-PG (HPV 6, 11 — warts), 2016 AIIMS (nonavalent vaccine)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A 3-day-old infant of a mother with no antenatal care has cataract, patent ductus arteriosus and sensorineural deafness. The virus responsible belongs to the family
explanation:
Congenital rubella syndrome gives the triad of cataract, deafness and PDA, and risk is highest in the first trimester. Diagnosis in the newborn is rubella IgM or PCR. The vaccine is live attenuated, so it is avoided in pregnancy.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (congenital rubella triad), 2020 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (rubella family)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A child has fever, coryza, conjunctivitis and small white spots on the buccal mucosa, followed by a rash spreading from behind the ears. A serious late complication of this infection is
explanation:
SSPE appears 7–10 years after measles, with raised measles antibody in CSF. Measles is a single-stranded, negative-sense, enveloped RNA paramyxovirus. Vitamin A reduces mortality.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (Koplik spots — measles, enveloped ssRNA)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A child with sickle cell disease develops a sudden fall in haemoglobin with a reticulocyte count near zero. The virus responsible attaches to
options: The P antigen (globoside) on erythroid progenitors
explanation:
Parvovirus B19 is a small, non-enveloped single-stranded DNA virus. It also causes erythema infectiosum ("slapped cheek"), arthropathy in adults and non-immune hydrops fetalis.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (aplastic crisis — parvovirus), 2022 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (tropism for erythroid progenitors), 2022 INI-CET (slapped cheek, red cell aplasia), 2021 INI-CET (B19 features)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A 6-month-old has vomiting and profuse watery diarrhoea. Electron microscopy shows a wheel-shaped virus. The enterotoxin responsible acts by
options: Raising cyclic AMP as cholera toxin does
Acting as NSP4, a viral enterotoxin that raises intracellular calcium
explanation:
Rotavirus is a double-stranded, segmented RNA virus. It is diagnosed by antigen detection in stool (ELISA or latex). Live oral rotavirus vaccine is part of the national schedule.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (NSP4 enterotoxin), 2019 NEET-PG (wheel-shaped virus), 2023 NEET-PG (antigen detection in stool)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The commonest cause of outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in adults, on cruise ships and in institutions, is
explanation:
Norovirus is a non-enveloped, single-stranded RNA calicivirus with a very low infective dose and a short incubation (24–48 hours). Alcohol rubs are relatively ineffective against it, so hand washing and hypochlorite are used.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (commonest viral diarrhoea in adults — norovirus)
exam: 2015 AIIMS (commonest viral diarrhoea in adults — norovirus)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each enterovirus with the illness it classically causes.

| Virus | Illness |
|---|---|
| 1. Coxsackievirus A16 | a. Acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis |
| 2. Enterovirus 70 | b. Aseptic meningitis with a maculopapular rash |
| 3. Coxsackievirus B | c. Hand, foot and mouth disease |
| 4. Echovirus | d. Pleurodynia and myocarditis |
explanation:
Enteroviruses are the commonest cause of aseptic meningitis, which gives lymphocytic CSF with normal or near-normal glucose. Enterovirus 71 causes hand, foot and mouth disease with neurological complications.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2016 AIIMS (hand foot mouth — Coxsackie A16), 2020 INI-CET (enterovirus 70), 2020 INI-CET (CSF picture — echovirus)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The INCUBATION period of a disease is best defined as the interval between
options: Exposure and the onset of the first symptoms
Exposure and the appearance of antibodies
The onset of symptoms and recovery
Infection in one case and the onset of symptoms in a second case
explanation:
Option B is the window period, and option D is the serial interval. Useful figures: hepatitis A 15–45 days, varicella 14–21 days, measles about 10 days, and lymphogranuloma venereum 10–30 days.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (match — incubation periods), 2016 AIIMS (LGV incubation)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A patient has had fever for 6 days with retro-orbital pain and petechiae. NS1 antigen is now negative. The appropriate test is
explanation:
NS1 and RT-PCR are useful in the first 5 days. IgM appears from day 5 and is the test of choice after that, which is why an antibody ELISA is not helpful on day 3.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (fever >5 days, petechiae — IgM capture ELISA), 2015 AIIMS (ELISA not helpful at day 3)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Severe dengue on a second infection with a different serotype is explained by
options: Antibody-dependent enhancement, in which non-neutralising antibody helps the virus enter Fc receptor-bearing cells
explanation:
Plasma leakage from increased capillary permeability, not bleeding alone, defines severe dengue. Warning signs include persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, mucosal bleeding and lethargy.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (ADE in dengue haemorrhagic fever), 2023 INI-CET (warning sign — vomiting)
exam: 2015 AIIMS (ADE in dengue haemorrhagic fever), 2023 INI-CET

subject: Microbiology
stem: In the transmission cycle of Japanese encephalitis, humans are
options: Dead-end hosts, because viraemia is low and brief
explanation:
Ardeid water birds are the natural reservoir, pigs are the amplifying host, and *Culex tritaeniorhynchus* is the vector, which is why cases cluster near rice fields and piggeries. A live attenuated vaccine (SA 14-14-2) is used in endemic districts.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (match — JE hosts and vector), 2020 NEET-PG (humans are dead-end hosts), 2014 AIIMS (Culex, pigs, birds)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (match — JE hosts and vector), 2020 NEET-PG (hu

subject: Microbiology
stem: A patient bitten by a dog 2 months ago develops hydrophobia and aerophobia. The most appropriate antemortem test is
options: RT-PCR on saliva, with nuchal skin biopsy immunofluorescence
explanation:
Corneal impression smears can also be used but are less sensitive. Negri bodies in hippocampal neurons are a postmortem finding. Rabies is essentially always fatal once symptoms begin, so post-exposure prophylaxis is what matters.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (corneal scraping — RT-PCR), 2020 INI-CET (most fatal virus — rabies)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A person with a deep bite from a stray dog, who has never been vaccinated, should receive
options: Rabies immunoglobulin infiltrated into the wound plus a full vaccine course, after washing with soap and water
Observation of the dog for 10 days before any action
explanation:
This is category III exposure. Washing for 15 minutes with soap and water is the single most effective first step. Previously vaccinated people need only two booster doses and no immunoglobulin.
> `VIROLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (rabies fatality), 2015 AIIMS (rabies diagnosis)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Antigenic shift in influenza A is caused by
options: Point mutations in the haemagglutinin gene
Reassortment of genome segments between two different strains infecting one cell
explanation:
The influenza A genome has 8 segments, which allows reassortment and causes pandemics. Antigenic drift (point mutations) causes seasonal epidemics and requires annual vaccine updates. Oseltamivir inhibits neuraminidase.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (influenza life cycle), 2017 AIIMS (oseltamivir — neuraminidase inhibitor), 2015 AIIMS (bird flu drugs)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Nipah virus outbreaks in India are linked to
options: Fruit bats, with contaminated date palm sap and person-to-person spread
explanation:
*Pteropus* bats are the reservoir. Nipah causes encephalitis and respiratory illness with high mortality, and nosocomial transmission is well documented, so strict isolation and PPE are needed.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (fruit bats, encephalitis — Nipah)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which statement about Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever is correct?
options: It is transmitted only by mosquitoes
It has never been reported from India
It is spread by Hyalomma ticks and by contact with blood of infected animals or patients
It is caused by a DNA virus
explanation:
Cases have been reported from Gujarat and Rajasthan. It is a segmented negative-sense RNA virus (Nairoviridae), and nosocomial outbreaks among health workers are well recognised. Ribavirin may be used.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (CCHF reported from India — T/F), 2014 AIIMS (haemorrhagic fever viruses)
exam: 2015 AIIMS (CCHF reported from India — T/F), 2014 AIIMS (hae

subject: Microbiology
stem: The vector of Zika, chikungunya and dengue in India is
explanation:
*Aedes* is a daytime biter that breeds in clean stored water, so control focuses on removing household breeding sites. Zika in pregnancy causes microcephaly, and it can also be transmitted sexually.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (Zika vector — Aedes aegypti)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which measure has NOT been shown to prevent COVID-19?
explanation:
Randomised trials showed no benefit from ivermectin, and it was removed from the national guidelines. SARS-CoV-2 is a positive-sense RNA virus diagnosed by RT-PCR, which needs a reverse transcription step.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (COVID preventive measures — not ivermectin), 2021 INI-CET (RNA viruses — RT-PCR)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which group is NOT conventionally classified as a "high-risk" group for HIV in India's national programme?
options: Men who have sex with men
explanation:
Truck drivers and migrant workers are classified as "bridge populations", not core high-risk groups. Targeted interventions are directed at the three core groups plus transgender people.
> `VIROLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (HIV high-risk group does not include truck drivers)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (HIV high-risk group does not include truck dri

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which component is absent from the cell wall of Mucorales, which explains why the 1,3-β-D-glucan assay is negative in mucormycosis?
explanation:
Mucorales have chitin and chitosan but little β-glucan. Cryptococcus is also negative because of its thick capsule. The assay is useful for candida, aspergillus and *Pneumocystis*. Echinocandins, which block glucan synthesis, do not work against mucormycosis.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (layer absent in mucor), 2020 INI-CET (fungal cell wall), 2014 AIIMS (1,3 β-D-glucan — invasive candidiasis)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (layer absent in mucor), 2020 INI-CET (fungal c

subject: Microbiology
stem: A man with poorly controlled diabetes and recent steroid use has facial pain, black necrotic turbinates and orbital swelling. Biopsy shows broad, aseptate hyphae with wide-angle branching. First-line treatment is
options: Liposomal amphotericin B with urgent surgical debridement
explanation:
Mucormycosis is angioinvasive, causing thrombosis and infarction, so antifungals alone cannot reach devitalised tissue. Posaconazole and isavuconazole are step-down options. Voriconazole has no activity and may even predispose to it.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (post-COVID steroid, aseptate hyphae — mucor), 2021 NEET-PG (DOC amphotericin B), 2016 AIIMS (mucormycosis drugs)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A neutropenic patient after chemotherapy has a halo sign on CT chest. Galactomannan is positive. Biopsy would show
explanation:
Invasive aspergillosis. Galactomannan is a cell-wall antigen used for diagnosis and monitoring. Voriconazole is the drug of choice. *Aspergillus* also causes mycotic endocarditis and aspergilloma.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (galactomannan — invasive aspergillosis), 2022 INI-CET (GMS — septate dichotomous), 2018 NEET-PG / 2015 AIIMS (acute-angle branching)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A germ tube test is performed by incubating yeast in serum at 37 °C for 2 hours. A positive result shows a filament with no constriction at its base, which identifies
explanation:
The absence of a constriction separates a true germ tube from a pseudohypha. *C. albicans* also forms chlamydospores on cornmeal agar. CHROMagar separates species by colour, and *C. krusei* is intrinsically resistant to fluconazole.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (germ tube formation), 2022 NEET-PG (budding yeast with pseudohyphae), 2020 NEET-PG (candida CHROMagar)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A patient on broad-spectrum antibiotics with a central venous catheter grows budding yeasts from blood. Management includes
options: Observation, since it is a contaminant
explanation:
Candidaemia always needs treatment, with removal of the infected line and fundoscopy to exclude endophthalmitis. Echinocandins are first-line while the species is identified.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (CVC infection — Candida), 2022 INI-CET (C. krusei resistant to fluconazole)

subject: Microbiology
stem: India ink preparation of CSF shows yeast cells with a wide clear halo. The best test for monitoring and confirming this infection is
options: Cryptococcal capsular polysaccharide antigen (CrAg) in CSF and serum
explanation:
CrAg latex agglutination or lateral flow assay is highly sensitive. The capsule is mucicarmine-positive. Treatment is amphotericin B with flucytosine, then fluconazole. Raised intracranial pressure needs repeated lumbar punctures.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2014 AIIMS (India ink — Cryptococcus), 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (mucicarmine stain), 2024 INI-CET (Cryptococcus — respiratory entry), 2020 INI-CET (Cryptococcus features)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The primary route by which Cryptococcus enters the human body is
options: Inhalation of desiccated yeast cells from soil contaminated with bird droppings
explanation:
Infection starts in the lung and may stay subclinical, then disseminates to the CNS when cell-mediated immunity falls. *C. neoformans* is linked to pigeon droppings; *C. gattii* to eucalyptus trees and affects immunocompetent people.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (Cryptococcus causes respiratory infection — T/F), 2020 INI-CET (Cryptococcus characteristics)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each dimorphic fungus with its tissue form.

| Fungus | Tissue form |
|---|---|
| 1. Histoplasma capsulatum | a. Spherule containing endospores |
| 2. Blastomyces dermatitidis | b. Small intracellular yeasts within macrophages |
| 3. Coccidioides immitis | c. Yeasts with a "pilot wheel" of multiple buds |
| 4. Paracoccidioides brasiliensis | d. Broad-based budding yeast |
explanation:
Dimorphic fungi grow as moulds at 25 °C and as yeasts (or spherules) at 37 °C. *Talaromyces marneffei* is the exception that divides by fission and produces a red pigment on culture.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (dimorphic fungi), 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (broad-based budding — blastomycosis), 2015 AIIMS (dimorphic examples), 2020 NEET-PG (Talaromyces)

subject: Microbiology
stem: "Desert rheumatism" with fever, erythema nodosum and arthralgia after dust exposure in an endemic area is caused by
explanation:
Arthroconidia in dry soil are inhaled and form spherules in tissue. Cultures are highly infectious for laboratory staff and need BSL-3. Most infections resolve without treatment.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (desert rheumatism — Coccidioides), 2024 INI-CET (dimorphic fungi)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A gardener pricked by a rose thorn develops a nodule that ulcerates, followed by a chain of nodules along the lymphatics of the forearm. The organism and treatment are
explanation:
This is lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis, acquired by traumatic inoculation. Culture shows rosette-like (flower-like) arrangements of conidia. Potassium iodide is a cheap alternative; amphotericin B is for disseminated disease.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (traumatic inoculation — Sporothrix), 2021 INI-CET (rosette-like conidia — sporotrichosis)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A farmer has a slowly growing warty plaque on the foot. Biopsy shows thick-walled, dark brown, septate cells that divide by splitting. These are
explanation:
Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous (pigmented) fungi such as *Fonsecaea*, *Cladosporium* and *Phialophora*. Phaeohyphomycosis, by contrast, shows pigmented hyphae rather than muriform cells.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (copper penny bodies, 2X), 2018 NEET-PG / 2016 AIIMS (chromoblastomycosis), 2021 INI-CET (Cladosporium)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A farmer has a swollen foot with multiple sinuses discharging granules. The key reason to distinguish eumycetoma from actinomycetoma is that
options: Actinomycetoma responds to antibacterials (cotrimoxazole with amikacin), whereas eumycetoma needs antifungals and often surgery
explanation:
Actinomycetoma is caused by bacteria (*Nocardia*, *Actinomadura*, *Streptomyces*) and eumycetoma by true fungi (*Madurella*). Granule colour and microscopy of the grains guide the distinction.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (mycetoma caused by both bacteria and fungi), 2020 INI-CET (discharging sinuses on foot — mycetoma), 2018 NEET-PG (white granules — Nocardia)
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (mycetoma caused by both bacteria and fungi), 2

subject: Microbiology
stem: A woman from south India has a friable, red, polypoid mass in the nose that bleeds easily. Histology shows large sporangia packed with endospores. The agent
options: Cannot be cultured on artificial media and is treated surgically with dapsone
explanation:
*Rhinosporidium seeberi* is now classified among aquatic protists (Mesomycetozoea), not true fungi. It is linked to bathing in stagnant ponds, and recurrence after excision is common.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (red polypoid nasal mass — Rhinosporidium), 2015 AIIMS (aquatic protistan protozoa)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The hair perforation test is used to separate
explanation:
*T. mentagrophytes* perforates hair and is urease-positive. *T. rubrum* does not perforate and produces a deep red pigment on the reverse of the colony with pencil-shaped macroconidia.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (hair perforation — T. mentagrophytes), 2020 NEET-PG (red pigment, pencil-shaped macroconidia — T. rubrum)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which dermatophyte genus does NOT invade hair?
explanation:
*Epidermophyton floccosum* infects skin and nails only. *Microsporum* infects skin and hair but not nails. *Trichophyton* infects all three. Dermatophytes cause annular lesions with central clearing.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (annular lesions — Trichophyton, Epidermophyton, Microsporum), 2017 AIIMS (dermatophytosis)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Scrapings from hypopigmented scaly macules on the trunk show short hyphae with clusters of round yeasts ("spaghetti and meatballs"). The organism is
explanation:
Pityriasis versicolor shows golden-yellow fluorescence under Wood's lamp. *Malassezia* is lipophilic, so culture needs olive oil overlay. In neonates on intravenous lipid it can cause catheter-related fungaemia.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (hair perforation test), 2020 NEET-PG (itch in axilla — T. rubrum)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A person with advanced HIV has progressive breathlessness with a normal-looking chest X-ray and marked desaturation on exertion. Silver stain of induced sputum shows crescent-shaped cysts. Treatment is
options: Cotrimoxazole, with steroids if hypoxia is severe
explanation:
*Pneumocystis jirovecii* cannot be cultured and is shown by GMS, toluidine blue or immunofluorescence. Prophylaxis is given when the CD4 count falls below 200. Infection does not confer lasting immunity.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (GMS crescent-shaped cysts — Pneumocystis), 2018 AIIMS (no lifelong immunity — T/F)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each antifungal with its mechanism.

| Antifungal | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Amphotericin B | a. Inhibits 1,3-β-D-glucan synthase |
| 2. Fluconazole | b. Converted to 5-fluorouracil, blocking nucleic acid synthesis |
| 3. Caspofungin | c. Binds ergosterol and forms membrane pores |
| 4. Flucytosine | d. Inhibits lanosterol 14-α-demethylase, blocking ergosterol synthesis |
explanation:
Flucytosine does not act on microtubules; griseofulvin does. Terbinafine inhibits squalene epoxidase. Echinocandins have no activity against *Cryptococcus*, which has little glucan in its wall.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (flucytosine — microtubules, false), 2022 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (amphotericin — pores), 2024 INI-CET (fungal wall components)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Voriconazole is given with a loading dose because
options: A loading dose reaches steady-state concentrations quickly, which matters in invasive aspergillosis
It has a very short half-life
explanation:
Voriconazole shows non-linear kinetics and wide variability, so therapeutic drug monitoring is used. Visual disturbances and photosensitivity are characteristic side effects.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (voriconazole loading dose — T/F), 2022 NEET-PG (DOC invasive aspergillosis)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Sabouraud dextrose agar is made selective for fungi mainly by
options: A low pH (about 5.6) with added antibiotics such as chloramphenicol and cycloheximide
explanation:
Cycloheximide suppresses saprophytic moulds but also inhibits *Cryptococcus* and some *Aspergillus*, so plates without it are set up in parallel. *Histoplasma* does grow on SDA, as the mould form at 25 °C.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (Histoplasma does not grow on SDA — false, 2X)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (Histoplasma does not grow on SDA — false, 2X)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A potassium hydroxide (KOH) mount is used for skin, hair and nail samples because KOH
options: Digests keratin and clears the background so hyphae become visible
explanation:
A 10–20% solution is used for skin and 40% for nails. Adding calcofluor white and viewing with fluorescence greatly increases sensitivity, and lactophenol cotton blue is used for culture mounts.
> `MYCOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (saline versus iodine wet mount), 2024 INI-CET (laboratory methods)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (saline versus iodine wet mount), 2024 INI-CET

subject: Microbiology
stem: Late trophozoites and schizonts of Plasmodium falciparum are rarely seen in a peripheral smear because
options: They are destroyed by the spleen
Infected red cells express knob proteins (PfEMP-1) and sequester in capillaries
They are too small to see
explanation:
Cytoadherence to endothelium underlies cerebral malaria. The smear usually shows only ring forms and banana-shaped gametocytes. High parasitaemia with multiply-infected cells is another feature.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (assertion — sequestration, 2X), 2022 NEET-PG (crescent gametocytes), 2020 NEET-PG (ring forms)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The best method to confirm the species of malaria parasite is
options: A rapid antigen test for HRP-2
explanation:
The thick film concentrates parasites and is better for detecting low parasitaemia; the thin film preserves red cell morphology, which is what allows speciation and parasite counting. HRP-2 tests detect only *P. falciparum* and stay positive for weeks after cure.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (best test for speciation — Giemsa thin smear)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (best test for speciation — Giemsa thin smear)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which feature distinguishes P. vivax from P. falciparum on a smear?
options: Enlarged infected red cells with Schüffner's dots and all stages present
explanation:
*P. vivax* invades reticulocytes through the Duffy antigen, so parasitaemia stays low. Its hypnozoites cause relapses, which need primaquine or tafenoquine for radical cure after testing for G6PD deficiency.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (ring forms, schizonts, spherical gametocytes — P. vivax), 2021 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (Anopheles vector)
exam: 2015 AIIMS (ring forms, schizonts, spherical gametocytes — P

subject: Microbiology
stem: Transfusion-transmitted malaria has a shorter incubation period than mosquito-borne malaria because
options: The dose of parasites is higher
The transfused blood contains erythrocytic stages, so the liver phase is bypassed
explanation:
For the same reason, transfusion-transmitted *P. vivax* does not relapse: no hypnozoites are formed, so primaquine is unnecessary.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (shorter incubation — trophozoites in blood)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A traveller returning from Africa has cerebral malaria with altered sensorium. The correct treatment is
explanation:
Intravenous artesunate reduces mortality compared with quinine in severe malaria. Oral ACT is used only for uncomplicated malaria. Primaquine is given as a single low dose as a gametocytocide, but it is not the treatment for the acute attack.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (falciparum with seizures — IV artesunate), 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (artemether–lumefantrine), 2023 INI-CET (primaquine not for uncomplicated malaria)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A young man has fever with hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia. Amastigotes are seen inside macrophages. The most sensitive non-invasive field test is
explanation:
Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is confirmed by rK39 or by splenic or bone marrow aspirate, with splenic aspirate the most sensitive but riskiest. Buffy coat improves yield from blood. Liposomal amphotericin B is first-line in India.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (LD bodies — rK39, 5X), 2021 INI-CET (buffy coat), 2021 INI-CET (Leishmania in Kupffer cells)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The vector of visceral leishmaniasis in India is
explanation:
The female sandfly breeds in cracks in mud walls, which is why indoor residual spraying is the main control measure. Humans are the only reservoir in the Indian form, which is why elimination is feasible.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (kinetoplast organism — Leishmania), 2021 INI-CET (LD bodies in buffy coat)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A person with HIV and a CD4 count of 60 has profuse watery diarrhoea. Modified acid-fast stain of stool shows 4–6 µm round oocysts. The organism is
explanation:
Size separates the coccidia: *Cryptosporidium* 4–6 µm, *Cyclospora* 8–10 µm (autofluorescent), *Cystoisospora* 20–30 µm and ellipsoidal. Cotrimoxazole treats the latter two; nitazoxanide plus immune reconstitution is used for cryptosporidiosis.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (4–6 µm Kinyoun-positive — Cryptosporidium, 4X), 2016 AIIMS (10–30 µm — Cystoisospora), 2017 AIIMS (DOC for Isospora)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A man has right upper quadrant pain and a single large liver abscess containing "anchovy sauce" material. The most useful test is
explanation:
Stool microscopy is often negative in amoebic liver abscess because the bowel infection may have cleared. Pus is sterile on bacterial culture and contains few amoebae, since they lie at the abscess wall. Treatment is metronidazole followed by a luminal amoebicide.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (dysentery with right lobe liver abscess), 2020 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (E. histolytica life cycle, 4X)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (dysentery with right lobe liver abscess), 2020

subject: Microbiology
stem: Amoebic dysentery is distinguished from bacillary dysentery on stool examination by
options: Few pus cells with charcot-leyden crystals and red cell-containing trophozoites in amoebic dysentery
Absence of blood in amoebic dysentery
Presence of macrophages only in amoebic dysentery
explanation:
Amoebic stools are copious and foul with few leucocytes. Bacillary dysentery gives small-volume stools packed with neutrophils. Erythrophagocytosis by trophozoites identifies *E. histolytica* rather than the harmless *E. dispar*.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (high frequency low volume diarrhoea with leucocytes)
exam: 2016 AIIMS (high frequency low volume diarrhoea with leucocy

subject: Microbiology
stem: A teenager develops fulminant meningoencephalitis days after swimming in a warm freshwater pond. CSF wet mount shows motile amoebae with blunt pseudopods. The organism and its portal of entry are
options: Naegleria fowleri — through the cribriform plate from the nasal mucosa
explanation:
Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis is rapidly fatal; amphotericin B with miltefosine is used. *Acanthamoeba* causes a slower granulomatous encephalitis and keratitis in contact lens users, and has cyst and trophozoite forms.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (swimming, eruptive pseudopods — Naegleria), 2023 NEET-PG (contact lens keratitis — Acanthamoeba), 2023 INI-CET (two morphological forms)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A woman has a frothy, foul-smelling greenish vaginal discharge with a strawberry cervix. Wet mount shows jerky motile organisms. Treatment should
options: Be given to the patient only
Include the sexual partner, with oral metronidazole for both
explanation:
Trichomoniasis is sexually transmitted, so untreated partners cause reinfection. The organism exists only as a trophozoite with no cyst stage, and vaginal pH is above 4.5.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (strawberry cervix — metronidazole), 2022 NEET-PG (twitching motility), 2018 AIIMS (pear-shaped trophozoites)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A child has foul-smelling, fatty diarrhoea with abdominal bloating after a camping trip. Stool examination is negative three times. The next best test is
options: Repeat stool microscopy a fourth time
Stool antigen detection (ELISA) or duodenal aspirate
explanation:
*Giardia* is shed intermittently, so microscopy may miss it; the string (Entero-test) or duodenal aspirate improves yield. It causes malabsorption by covering the mucosa, and is common in IgA deficiency. Treatment is metronidazole or tinidazole.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (two morphological forms — Giardia), 2018 AIIMS (histology in diarrhoea — giardiasis)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A pregnant woman's serology shows Toxoplasma IgG positive and IgM positive. The test that best establishes whether the infection is recent is
explanation:
IgM can persist for a year or more, so it cannot date the infection. High avidity IgG indicates infection more than 3–4 months earlier, which effectively excludes recent infection in early pregnancy. Amniotic fluid PCR confirms fetal infection.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (Sabin–Feldman dye test), 2023 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (congenital toxoplasmosis triad)

subject: Microbiology
stem: The infective stage of Toxoplasma gondii acquired from cat faeces is the
explanation:
Cats are the definitive host. Oocysts need 1–5 days in the environment to sporulate, so daily litter changing reduces risk. Eating undercooked meat transmits bradyzoites. Congenital infection gives chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus and diffuse intracranial calcification.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (infective form in cat faeces — oocyst), 2023 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (congenital triad)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (infective form in cat faeces — oocyst), 2023 N

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which parasite can complete its entire life cycle within one human host, causing hyperinfection in immunosuppressed patients?
explanation:
Rhabditiform larvae can become infective filariform larvae inside the bowel and reinvade (autoinfection). Steroids or HTLV-1 infection trigger hyperinfection with Gram-negative sepsis. The female reproduces by parthenogenesis, and ivermectin is the drug of choice.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (rhabditiform larva, parthenogenesis, 5X), 2023 INI-CET (autoinfection), 2022 INI-CET (self-fertilisation), 2022 NEET-PG (larvae in BAL)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which parasite is NOT a recognised cause of autoinfection?
explanation:
*Ascaris* eggs must embryonate in soil for 2–3 weeks before they are infective, so direct reinfection is impossible. *Enterobius* causes retroinfection, *H. nana* autoinfects in the gut, and *T. solium* eggs can cause internal autoinfection leading to cysticercosis.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (autoinfection — not ascaris), 2024 INI-CET (most ascariasis asymptomatic)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each helminth with its characteristic egg.

| Helminth | Egg |
|---|---|
| 1. Trichuris trichiura | a. Plano-convex, flattened on one side |
| 2. Enterobius vermicularis | b. Barrel-shaped with mucoid plugs at both poles |
| 3. Ascaris lumbricoides | c. Hexacanth embryo with polar filaments |
| 4. Hymenolepis nana | d. Round with a thick albuminous mamillated coat |
explanation:
Hookworm eggs are oval, non-bile-stained, with a thin hyaline shell and a segmented ovum of four blastomeres. Pinworm eggs are collected on a cellophane tape swab in the morning.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (match — H. nana, Ascaris, hookworm, Taenia), 2024 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (barrel-shaped egg — Trichuris, 5X), 2023 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (plano-convex egg — Enterobius), 2015 AIIMS (hookworm egg)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (match — H. nana, Ascaris, hookworm, Taenia), 2

subject: Microbiology
stem: Heavy whipworm infection in a child classically presents with
options: Rectal prolapse with chronic bloody mucoid diarrhoea
explanation:
*Trichuris trichiura* threads its thin anterior end into the colonic mucosa. Infection is acquired by ingesting embryonated eggs from contaminated food or water, with no larval migration through the lungs.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (rectal prolapse, barrel egg — route of infection, 5X)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Pulmonary symptoms with transient infiltrates and eosinophilia (Löffler syndrome) occur in infections where larvae migrate through the lungs. Which worm does NOT do this?
explanation:
Pinworm larvae stay in the gut. The others follow a heart–lung migration, so pneumonitis is the commonest presentation during larval migration. Hookworm causes iron deficiency anaemia, and the Chandler index measures community hookworm load.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (larval migration — pneumonitis), 2016 AIIMS (Chandler index — hookworm), 2016 AIIMS (soil-transmitted helminths)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A man has a single large cyst in the right lobe of the liver. Aspirate shows brood capsules and protoscolices. The definitive host of this parasite is
explanation:
*Echinococcus granulosus* lives in the dog's small intestine; humans and sheep are intermediate hosts. Treatment is albendazole with PAIR or surgery, taking care to avoid spillage, which can cause anaphylaxis and secondary cysts.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (brood capsules and protoscolices — Echinococcus), 2017 AIIMS (adult worm in dog)

subject: Microbiology
stem: A man who eats undercooked pork develops seizures. CT shows multiple small cystic lesions with scolices. The parasite stage responsible is
options: The adult tapeworm from eating cysticerci
The larval cysticercus, from ingesting Taenia solium eggs
explanation:
Eating undercooked pork gives intestinal taeniasis; swallowing eggs (faeco-oral, including autoinfection) gives neurocysticercosis. Treatment uses albendazole with corticosteroids started first to limit inflammation, plus antiepileptics.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (neurocysticercosis — steroids then antiparasitic), 2015 AIIMS (autoinfection — T. solium)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Which tapeworm competes for vitamin B₁₂ and can cause megaloblastic anaemia?
explanation:
The fish tapeworm is acquired from raw or undercooked freshwater fish and is the longest human tapeworm. Praziquantel is the drug of choice, with B₁₂ replacement where needed.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (pernicious anaemia — D. latum), 2016 AIIMS (praziquantel for H. nana)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Infection with Fasciola hepatica is acquired by
options: Eating aquatic plants such as watercress or water chestnut carrying metacercariae
explanation:
Snails are the first intermediate host. The flukes migrate to the bile ducts, causing right upper quadrant pain and eosinophilia. Triclabendazole is the drug of choice, unlike most other trematodes which respond to praziquantel.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (water calotrops — Fasciola), 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (life cycle — metacercariae on plants), 2022 INI-CET / 2023 INI-CET (DOC triclabendazole)

subject: Microbiology
stem:
Match each trematode with how it is acquired and the organ it affects.

| Fluke | Acquisition and site |
|---|---|
| 1. Clonorchis sinensis | a. Skin penetration by cercariae; bladder (haematuria) |
| 2. Paragonimus westermani | b. Raw freshwater fish; bile ducts, raises cholangiocarcinoma risk |
| 3. Schistosoma haematobium | c. Skin penetration; mesenteric veins and liver |
| 4. Schistosoma mansoni | d. Raw freshwater crab or crayfish; lung, mimics tuberculosis |
explanation:
*Clonorchis* and *Opisthorchis* are proven causes of cholangiocarcinoma. *Paragonimus* produces rusty-brown sputum and is often misdiagnosed as tuberculosis. *S. haematobium* is linked to squamous carcinoma of the bladder.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (Clonorchis — cholangiocarcinoma), 2020 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (crab, rusty sputum — Paragonimus)

subject: Microbiology
stem: Sheathed microfilariae with nuclei extending right up to the tip of the tail indicate
explanation:
*B. malayi* has two separate terminal nuclei at the tail tip, whereas *W. bancrofti* has a tail free of nuclei. Both are sheathed and show nocturnal periodicity, so blood is collected at night. *Onchocerca* microfilariae are unsheathed and found in skin snips.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (two nuclei at tail tip — B. malayi, 4X), 2017 AIIMS (filarial species)
exam: 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (two nuclei at tail tip — B. malay

subject: Microbiology
stem: In onchocerciasis, the rationale for giving doxycycline along with ivermectin is that doxycycline
options: Kills Wolbachia endosymbionts, which sterilises and eventually kills the adult worms
explanation:
Ivermectin kills microfilariae but not adults. Releasing *Wolbachia* from dying worms also drives the inflammatory Mazzotti reaction. Ivermectin is avoided where *Loa loa* is heavily present, because of encephalopathy.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (adult worms responsible in filarial disease), 2017 AIIMS (filarial species)
exam: 2018 AIIMS (adult worms responsible in filarial disease), 20

subject: Microbiology
stem: A patient with filariasis develops acute lymphangitis that spreads from the groin down the limb. This "retrograde" spread is characteristic because
options: The adult worms live in the lymphatics and lymph nodes, and inflammation travels away from them
explanation:
Bacterial lymphangitis spreads upwards (ascending) towards the nodes, whereas filarial lymphangitis spreads downwards. Repeated attacks with secondary bacterial infection lead to elephantiasis, which is managed by limb hygiene rather than antifilarials.
> `PARASITOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (adult worms responsible in filarial disease), 2017 AIIMS (filariasis species)
exam: 2018 AIIMS (adult worms responsible in filarial disease), 20

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A drug has a volume of distribution of 350 L and a clearance of 35 L/hour. Its elimination half-life is about
explanation:
t½ = 0.693 × Vd ÷ CL = 0.693 × 350 ÷ 35 = 6.93, about 7 hours. Forgetting the 0.693 factor gives the trap answer of 10 hours.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (digoxin half-life from Vd and clearance)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (digoxin half-life from Vd and clearance)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A drug with a target plasma concentration of 4 mg/L and a volume of distribution of 50 L is given orally with a bioavailability of 0.5. The loading dose required is
explanation:
Loading dose = (target concentration × Vd) ÷ bioavailability = (4 × 50) ÷ 0.5 = 400 mg. The loading dose depends on Vd, not on clearance; maintenance dose depends on clearance.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (factors in oral loading dose, 3X), 2015 AIIMS (loading dose depends on Vd)
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (factors in oral loading dose, 3

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A drug is eliminated with a clearance of 6 L/hour, and the target steady-state concentration is 5 mg/L. The maintenance dosing rate for an intravenous infusion is
explanation:
Dosing rate = clearance × target steady-state concentration = 6 × 5 = 30 mg/hour. Steady state is reached after about 4–5 half-lives whatever the dose.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (dosing rate = clearance × target concentration)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient's serum level of a drug is 8 µg/mL; the target is 1 µg/mL. The half-life is 12 hours. Assuming first-order elimination, therapy can be resumed after about
explanation:
Each half-life halves the concentration: 8 → 4 → 2 → 1, which is 3 half-lives, so 3 × 12 = 36 hours. In first-order kinetics, half-life is constant and does not change when the dose is doubled.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (digoxin 4 to 1 mg/dL, t½ 40 h — 80 h), 2020 INI-CET (first-order kinetics — half-life unchanged)
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (digoxin 4 to 1 mg/dL, t½ 40 h — 80 h), 2020 IN

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which pair of drugs follows ZERO-order (saturation) kinetics at therapeutic doses?
explanation:
In zero-order kinetics a constant **amount** is eliminated per unit time, so a small dose increase can cause a disproportionate rise in level and toxicity. Aspirin in overdose also shifts to zero order.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (first-order kinetics features), 2020 INI-CET (first-order half-life)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A weakly acidic drug such as aspirin is excreted faster when the urine is alkalinised because
options: The drug becomes more lipid soluble
The drug becomes more ionised in alkaline urine, so it cannot be reabsorbed across the tubular membrane
explanation:
Only un-ionised, lipid-soluble molecules diffuse back. This is ion trapping, and is why sodium bicarbonate is used in salicylate poisoning. Acidifying urine would similarly trap weak bases.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (alkalinisation helps excretion of salicylates), 2023 NEET-PG / 2020 NEET-PG (sodium bicarbonate in aspirin poisoning)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The pKa of a drug is the pH at which
options: Half the drug is ionised and half un-ionised
explanation:
Weak acids are largely un-ionised, and therefore absorbed, in the acidic stomach; weak bases are absorbed better in the alkaline intestine. In practice most absorption still occurs in the small intestine because of its vast surface area.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (pKa definition)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A drug that is extensively bound to plasma albumin will have
options: A high volume of distribution and rapid glomerular filtration
A low volume of distribution and reduced glomerular filtration
explanation:
Bound drug stays in the plasma compartment and is not filtered. Displacement interactions matter most for drugs that are highly bound with a narrow therapeutic index, such as warfarin and phenytoin. Weak acids bind albumin; weak bases bind α1-acid glycoprotein.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (high protein binding — less filtration), 2016 AIIMS (high binding — low Vd), 2020 INI-CET (weakly acidic drug binds albumin)
exam: 2017 AIIMS (high protein binding — less filtration), 2016 AI

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which sequence correctly ranks these drugs by increasing volume of distribution?
explanation:
Heparin is a large, highly bound molecule confined to plasma. Gentamicin distributes in extracellular fluid. Phenytoin enters total body water, and lipophilic haloperidol concentrates in tissues, giving a very large Vd.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (order by volume of distribution), 2014 AIIMS (low Vd meaning)
exam: 2018 AIIMS (order by volume of distribution), 2014 AIIMS (lo

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Phase I reactions of drug metabolism include
explanation:
Phase I introduces or exposes a functional group, usually through cytochrome P450, which generally makes the molecule more water-soluble. Phase II conjugation then adds a polar group. Some Phase I products are active or toxic, as with paracetamol's NAPQI.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (Phase I metabolism), 2018 AIIMS (CYP metabolism — increased water solubility)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient stabilised on warfarin is started on rifampicin. The expected effect and the reason are
options: Increased bleeding risk, because rifampicin inhibits CYP2C9
No change, because warfarin is renally cleared
Loss of anticoagulant effect, because rifampicin induces CYP enzymes and increases warfarin metabolism
Increased INR, because of displacement from albumin
explanation:
Enzyme induction takes days to develop and to wear off. Inducers include rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone and chronic alcohol. Inhibitors (macrolides, azoles, cimetidine, valproate) act within hours.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (carbamazepine plus azithromycin — toxicity), 2022 NEET-PG (zidovudine regimen — change rifampicin), 2016 AIIMS (enzyme inducers with warfarin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which measure best describes the EXTENT of absorption of an oral drug?
options: Area under the plasma concentration–time curve
explanation:
AUC reflects total exposure. Cmax and Tmax describe the rate of absorption. Bioavailability is the ratio of oral AUC to intravenous AUC. Two formulations are bioequivalent when AUC and Cmax fall within 80–125% of each other.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (best measure of extent of absorption — AUC)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (best measure of extent of absorption — AUC)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The therapeutic index is calculated as
explanation:
A larger value means a safer drug. Lithium, digoxin, warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline and aminoglycosides have narrow indices and need monitoring. Potency is the dose needed for an effect; efficacy is the maximum effect achievable.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG (drug safety — LD50/ED50, 3X), 2015 AIIMS (therapeutic index is a measure of safety), 2023 NEET-PG (potency versus efficacy)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Two drugs produce the same maximal response, but drug A achieves it at a lower dose than drug B. Drug A is
explanation:
Potency shifts the dose–response curve to the left; efficacy is the height of its plateau. Clinically, efficacy matters more, because a less potent drug can simply be given at a higher dose.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (drug A more potent but equally efficacious)
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (drug A more potent but equally efficacious)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A multicentre trial randomises 450 patients to a new drug or placebo, with both patients and investigators blinded, to establish efficacy. This is a
explanation:
Phase 1 assesses safety and kinetics in 20–80 healthy volunteers. Phase 2 looks at efficacy and dose-finding in a few hundred patients. Phase 3 is the large comparative trial before licensing. Phase 4 is post-marketing surveillance, which detects rare adverse effects.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (phase 3 trial, 3X), 2015 AIIMS (phase I aim — safety), 2014 AIIMS (post-marketing surveillance — phase IV)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A manufacturer labels a tablet as containing 500 mg of paracetamol, but assay shows only 200 mg. Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act this product is
explanation:
Schedule H lists drugs that may be sold only on a registered practitioner's prescription; Schedule X covers drugs needing stricter custody and record-keeping, such as ketamine. "Store in a cool place" means 8–15 °C.
> `GENERAL PHARMACOLOGY` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (counterfeit/misbranded, 3X), 2014 AIIMS (schedule H), 2021 INI-CET (schedule X — ketamine), 2022 INI-CET / 2016 AIIMS (cool place 8–15 °C)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each receptor with its principal signalling pathway.

| Receptor | Pathway |
|---|---|
| 1. β2 adrenergic | a. Gq — phospholipase C — IP3 and DAG |
| 2. α1 adrenergic | b. Gi — decreased cyclic AMP |
| 3. M2 muscarinic | c. Gs — adenylyl cyclase — increased cyclic AMP |
| 4. Nicotinic (NM) | d. Ligand-gated cation channel |
explanation:
Muscarinic receptors are G-protein coupled: M1, M3 and M5 use Gq, while M2 and M4 use Gi. Nicotinic receptors are ionotropic, which is why ganglionic and neuromuscular transmission is fast.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (GPCR example — muscarinic), 2021 NEET-PG (β2 via adenylate cyclase), 2016 AIIMS (phospholipase C via Gq), 2016 AIIMS (ganglionic transmission — nicotinic)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A farm worker is brought with pinpoint pupils, profuse salivation, bronchorrhoea, bradycardia and fasciculations. The immediate priority is
options: Atropine in escalating doses until secretions dry, with oxygen and airway support
explanation:
Death in organophosphate poisoning is from bronchial secretions and respiratory failure, so atropine is titrated to drying of secretions rather than to pupil size. Oximes reactivate acetylcholinesterase before ageing occurs, but they do not replace atropine.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (organophosphate poisoning — atropine, 3X), 2021 INI-CET (organophosphates — irreversible inhibitors), 2015 AIIMS (competitive and irreversible)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A young man has dilated pupils, dry flushed skin, fever, urinary retention and delirium after eating wild berries. The best supportive antidote is
explanation:
This is antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) poisoning. Physostigmine is a tertiary amine that crosses the blood–brain barrier, unlike neostigmine. Most cases need only supportive care and benzodiazepines, since physostigmine can cause bradycardia and seizures.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (dilated pupils, dry skin, staggering gait — datura), 2023 INI-CET (atropine does not cause miosis)
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (dilated pupils, dry skin, staggering gait — da

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient with myasthenia gravis deteriorates. Weakness improves briefly after edrophonium. This indicates
explanation:
In cholinergic crisis, edrophonium makes weakness worse and adds muscarinic features. Edrophonium has a very short action, which makes it suitable for this test. Long-term treatment uses pyridostigmine.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (ptosis improving with neostigmine/edrophonium), 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (edrophonium to differentiate crises)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which drug should be avoided in a patient with myasthenia gravis?
explanation:
Aminoglycosides reduce presynaptic acetylcholine release and block postsynaptic receptors. Other drugs to avoid are fluoroquinolones, macrolides, β-blockers, magnesium, phenytoin and quinine.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (neomycin contraindicated in myasthenia), 2020 INI-CET (drugs worsening myasthenia)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Dopamine infused at 2–5 µg/kg/min acts mainly on
options: D1 receptors, causing renal and mesenteric vasodilatation
explanation:
At 5–10 µg/kg/min β1 effects dominate, and above 10 µg/kg/min α1 vasoconstriction takes over. Fenoldopam is a selective D1 agonist used in hypertensive emergency with renal impairment. "Renal-dose" dopamine is no longer recommended for renal protection.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (dopamine β1 dose range), 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (dopamine at 8 µg/kg/min, 4X), 2024 INI-CET (fenoldopam — D1 agonism)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (dopamine β1 dose range), 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 A

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The first-line vasopressor in septic shock that persists after adequate fluid resuscitation is
explanation:
Noradrenaline raises systemic vascular resistance through α1 with less tachyarrhythmia than dopamine. Its predominant α effect raises systolic, diastolic and mean pressure while reflex vagal activity slows the heart. Vasopressin is added as a second agent.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (first-line vasopressor in septic shock), 2018 NEET-PG (raised SBP, DBP, MBP with bradycardia — noradrenaline)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient in anaphylaxis after an injection should receive adrenaline
options: 0.5 mg of 1:1000 intramuscularly into the anterolateral thigh
explanation:
Intramuscular injection into the thigh gives faster, more reliable absorption than subcutaneous. Adrenaline reverses the reaction through α1 vasoconstriction, β2 bronchodilatation and stabilisation of mast cells. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts only.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (ampicillin anaphylaxis — 0.5 mL of 1:1000 IM, 4X), 2018 AIIMS (adrenaline actions in anaphylaxis)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient pre-treated with phentolamine is given adrenaline and becomes hypotensive. This is because
options: α receptors are blocked, so the unopposed β2 vasodilator effect lowers blood pressure
explanation:
This is vasomotor reversal of Dale. It does not happen with noradrenaline, which has negligible β2 activity, so its pressor effect is only abolished, not reversed.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (vasomotor reversal of Dale)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A child stung by a scorpion has tachypnoea, sweating and pulmonary oedema with hypertension. The drug of choice is
explanation:
Scorpion venom causes a massive catecholamine surge. Prazosin, an α1 blocker, reduces afterload and preload and is the standard treatment in India. β-blockers alone would leave α effects unopposed.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (scorpion bite — prazosin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A man with benign prostatic hyperplasia and hypertension is started on an α1 blocker and faints after the first dose. This first-dose phenomenon is minimised by
options: Giving it with food in the morning
Giving the first dose at bedtime and starting low
explanation:
Postural hypotension results from sudden venous and arteriolar dilatation. Tamsulosin and silodosin are relatively uroselective (α1A) and cause less hypotension, but carry a risk of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (first-dose syncope — α blockers), 2021 NEET-PG (BPH with urgency — tamsulosin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on long-term clonidine stops it abruptly and develops headache, tachycardia and a hypertensive crisis. The mechanism is
options: Loss of central α2-mediated sympathetic inhibition with a surge of catecholamines
explanation:
Clonidine must be tapered. Its anticholinergic-like side effects (dry mouth, sedation, constipation) are a common reason patients stop it on their own. Apraclonidine and brimonidine are ocular α2 agonists.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (rebound hypertension on stopping clonidine; dry mouth leading to stopping), 2020 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (apraclonidine — α2 agonist)
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (rebound hypertension on stopping clonidine; dr

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each anti-glaucoma drug with its mechanism of lowering intraocular pressure.

| Drug | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Latanoprost | a. Reduces aqueous production by blocking β receptors |
| 2. Timolol | b. Reduces aqueous production by inhibiting carbonic anhydrase |
| 3. Dorzolamide | c. Increases uveoscleral outflow |
| 4. Pilocarpine | d. Increases trabecular outflow by contracting the ciliary muscle |
explanation:
Prostaglandin analogues cause iris hyperpigmentation (heterochromia), eyelash growth and periorbital changes, and are avoided in uveitis and cystoid macular oedema. Topical steroids **raise** intraocular pressure.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (latanoprost — uveoscleral outflow), 2024 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (avoid latanoprost in cystoid macular oedema, 3X), 2015 AIIMS (heterochromia), 2022 INI-CET (betamethasone does not lower IOP), 2020 INI-CET (avoid prostaglandin in uveitis)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: In acute angle-closure glaucoma, pilocarpine lowers pressure by
options: Constricting the pupil, which pulls the peripheral iris away from the trabecular meshwork
explanation:
Intravenous mannitol or acetazolamide is given first to reduce pressure, then pilocarpine, followed by laser iridotomy. Drugs with antimuscarinic action such as amitriptyline can precipitate an attack.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (mannitol plus pilocarpine, 4X), 2020 INI-CET (amitriptyline avoided in angle closure)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A diabetic with COPD develops postoperative urinary retention with no obstruction. A short-term option is
explanation:
Bethanechol is a muscarinic agonist resistant to cholinesterase that stimulates detrusor contraction. It is contraindicated in asthma, COPD, peptic ulcer and bladder outlet obstruction, so its use is limited and catheterisation is usually preferred.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (diabetes, COPD, retention — bethanechol)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: An elderly man with Alzheimer disease on donepezil develops urge incontinence. The preferred antimuscarinic is
explanation:
Trospium is a quaternary amine that does not cross the blood–brain barrier, and darifenacin is M3-selective, so both spare cognition. Oxybutynin worsens confusion in the elderly. Mirabegron, a β3 agonist, avoids antimuscarinic effects entirely.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (Alzheimer with incontinence — tolterodine), 2022 INI-CET / 2016 AIIMS (mirabegron — β3 agonist)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Paradoxical bronchoconstriction occasionally seen with ipratropium is attributed to
options: Blockade of presynaptic M2 autoreceptors, which increases acetylcholine release
explanation:
M2 autoreceptors normally limit further acetylcholine release. Tiotropium binds M3 for longer than M2 (kinetic selectivity), which reduces this problem and allows once-daily dosing.
> `AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (paradoxical bronchoconstriction — presynaptic M2 block)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each antiepileptic drug with its principal mechanism.

| Drug | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Lacosamide | a. Inhibits GAT-1 and blocks GABA reuptake |
| 2. Tiagabine | b. Blocks T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons |
| 3. Ethosuximide | c. Binds SV2A synaptic vesicle protein |
| 4. Levetiracetam | d. Enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels |
explanation:
Phenytoin and carbamazepine enhance fast inactivation of sodium channels, whereas lacosamide acts on slow inactivation. Vigabatrin irreversibly inhibits GABA transaminase and causes irreversible visual field constriction.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (lacosamide — slow inactivation), 2024 INI-CET (tiagabine — GAT-1), 2020 INI-CET (absence seizure drugs), 2015 AIIMS (vigabatrin and visual defect)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The antiepileptic with the highest risk of neural tube defects when taken in the first trimester is
explanation:
Valproate also lowers IQ in exposed children, and it is avoided in women of child-bearing potential unless there is no alternative. Lamotrigine and levetiracetam are the preferred options in pregnancy, with folic acid supplementation.
