> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (antiepileptic most associated with NTD — valproate), 2016 AIIMS (pregnant on antiepileptic — continue treatment)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (antiepileptic most associated with NTD — valpr

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman with bipolar disorder on valproate becomes drowsy with a normal ammonia-lowering workup except for a raised serum ammonia and normal liver enzymes. The explanation is
options: Valproate-induced hyperammonaemic encephalopathy, often through carnitine depletion
explanation:
This can occur with normal transaminases and therapeutic valproate levels. Treatment is to stop valproate and give L-carnitine. Valproate also causes hepatotoxicity, weight gain, tremor, alopecia and polycystic ovary syndrome in women.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (liver dysfunction and hyperammonaemia — valproate), 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (valproate and carbamazepine hepatotoxicity), 2015 AIIMS (gender-specific effect — PCOS)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient stable on carbamazepine is given an enzyme-inhibiting antibiotic and develops ataxia, diplopia and vomiting. The likely drug added is
explanation:
Macrolides (except azithromycin, which is a weak inhibitor) inhibit CYP3A4 and raise carbamazepine levels. Carbamazepine is also an auto-inducer of its own metabolism, so doses often need increasing in the first weeks.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (carbamazepine plus azithromycin — toxicity)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Compared with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine is more likely to cause
explanation:
Oxcarbazepine causes more SIADH-like hyponatraemia but less enzyme induction, fewer blood dyscrasias and fewer rashes. Severe cutaneous reactions to carbamazepine are strongly linked to HLA-B*1502 in people of Southeast Asian ancestry.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (hyponatraemia more with oxcarbazepine, 2X)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Fosphenytoin is preferred to intravenous phenytoin in status epilepticus because fosphenytoin
options: Has no cardiac effects at any dose
Can be given faster and causes less local tissue injury and fewer infusion-site reactions
explanation:
Phenytoin's propylene glycol vehicle causes phlebitis and purple glove syndrome. Fosphenytoin is water-soluble and converted to phenytoin. Both can cause hypotension and arrhythmia, so cardiac monitoring is still needed.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (high-dose fosphenytoin toxicity — T/F)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Thiopentone has a short duration of action after a single intravenous dose mainly because of
options: Redistribution from brain to muscle and fat
explanation:
Metabolism is slow, so repeated doses accumulate and the effect becomes prolonged. Propofol also terminates by redistribution but is cleared much faster, which allows infusion.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (thiopentone short action due to renal excretion — false)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (thiopentone short action due to renal excretio

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The intravenous induction agent most associated with adrenocortical suppression is
explanation:
Etomidate inhibits 11β-hydroxylase, so even a single dose can suppress cortisol for hours. It is still valued for cardiovascular stability in shocked patients. Ketamine raises blood pressure and causes emergence delirium, and is also used as a rapid-acting antidepressant.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (anaesthetic causing prolonged adrenal insufficiency), 2020 INI-CET (ketamine — rapid-acting antidepressant)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Sugammadex reverses rocuronium by
options: Encapsulating the drug molecule in plasma, forming an inactive complex
explanation:
This γ-cyclodextrin reverses even deep block within minutes and avoids the muscarinic effects of neostigmine, which must be given with glycopyrrolate or atropine. It works on aminosteroid blockers (rocuronium, vecuronium) but not on atracurium.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (fastest reversal of rocuronium — sugammadex), 2023 NEET-PG (vecuronium reversal), 2020 INI-CET (neostigmine reversal)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Atracurium and cisatracurium are preferred in hepatic and renal failure because they are eliminated by
options: Hofmann elimination, a spontaneous non-enzymatic degradation
explanation:
Cisatracurium is preferred to atracurium because it releases less histamine and produces less laudanosine. Succinylcholine, by contrast, is hydrolysed by plasma pseudocholinesterase.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 AIIMS (Hofmann elimination), 2018 AIIMS (cisatracurium preferred — less histamine), 2018 AIIMS (curare blocks ACh receptor)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient under halothane anaesthesia given succinylcholine develops masseter spasm, rising end-tidal CO2 and hyperthermia. The specific treatment is
options: Dantrolene, with cooling and supportive care
explanation:
Dantrolene blocks the ryanodine receptor and stops calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by volatile agents and succinylcholine in genetically susceptible people. Bromocriptine is used for neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (halothane with succinylcholine — malignant hyperthermia), 2018 AIIMS (dantrolene not a neuromuscular junction drug)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on fluoxetine is given an opioid for chronic pain and develops agitation, hyperreflexia, clonus and fever. Besides stopping the drugs, the specific agent used is
explanation:
Cyproheptadine is a 5-HT2A antagonist. Serotonin syndrome is distinguished from neuroleptic malignant syndrome by its rapid onset, clonus and hyperreflexia, whereas NMS has lead-pipe rigidity and evolves over days. Tramadol, pethidine, methadone, linezolid and MAO inhibitors are common precipitants.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (sertraline with MAOI — cyproheptadine), 2023 INI-CET (fluoxetine with methadone — QT prolongation)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which antidepressant is most likely to be chosen when sexual dysfunction is a major concern?
explanation:
Mirtazapine blocks presynaptic α2 and 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors, so it causes little sexual dysfunction and also improves sleep and appetite, at the cost of sedation and weight gain. Bupropion is the other option with minimal sexual effects.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (least sexual side effect — mirtazapine), 2021 NEET-PG (depression with low libido — mirtazapine)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Abrupt withdrawal of which antidepressant most often causes dizziness, anxiety and electric-shock sensations?
explanation:
Short half-life and absence of an active long-lived metabolite make discontinuation symptoms prominent with venlafaxine and paroxetine. Fluoxetine's long-acting metabolite norfluoxetine effectively self-tapers.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (discontinuation syndrome — venlafaxine), 2021 INI-CET (vilazodone — novel antidepressant), 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (SNRIs)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient who has taken an overdose of a tricyclic antidepressant has a widened QRS. The immediate treatment is
explanation:
Bicarbonate overcomes sodium-channel blockade by raising pH and sodium load, narrowing the QRS and preventing arrhythmia. Tricyclic overdose causes the "three Cs": coma, convulsions and cardiotoxicity, plus antimuscarinic features such as mydriasis and hyperthermia.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (TCA poisoning — IV sodium bicarbonate), 2023 INI-CET (features of TCA poisoning — not hypothermia), 2017 AIIMS (TCA side effects)
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (TCA poisoning — IV sodium bicarbonate), 2023 I

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Chlorpromazine causes postural hypotension, sedation and dry mouth because it also blocks
explanation:
Low-potency typical antipsychotics have more autonomic effects and fewer extrapyramidal effects; high-potency drugs such as haloperidol are the reverse. Risperidone causes the greatest rise in prolactin.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (chlorpromazine — H1, muscarinic, α1), 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (maximum prolactin — risperidone)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A young man on risperidone develops a sustained upward deviation of the eyes and neck stiffness a day after starting treatment. The correct management is
options: Parenteral promethazine or an anticholinergic such as benzhexol
explanation:
Acute dystonia (including oculogyric crisis) appears within hours to days and responds quickly to anticholinergics or antihistamines. Metoclopramide is a common non-psychiatric cause. Tardive dyskinesia, by contrast, appears after months and is worsened by anticholinergics.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (risperidone — fixed upward gaze, promethazine), 2022 NEET-PG / 2015 AIIMS (metoclopramide causing dystonia), 2019 NEET-PG (benzhexol), 2020 NEET-PG (fluphenazine parkinsonism — trihexyphenidyl)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Clozapine is reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and requires regular monitoring of
explanation:
Agranulocytosis occurs in about 1%. Clozapine also causes myocarditis, seizures, weight gain, metabolic syndrome and, paradoxically, hypersalivation despite its antimuscarinic profile. It has the lowest risk of extrapyramidal effects.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (clozapine side effect needing monitoring), 2021 INI-CET (sialorrhoea — clozapine)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on lithium who has been fasting presents with coarse tremor, ataxia, confusion and seizures. The most useful immediate investigation and definitive treatment are
options: Serum lithium level; haemodialysis if severely raised
explanation:
Lithium is cleared entirely by the kidney, so dehydration, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and thiazides precipitate toxicity. Haemodialysis is effective because lithium is a small, unbound ion with a low volume of distribution. Fine tremor is acceptable within the therapeutic range of about 0.6–1.2 mEq/L.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (lithium with coarse tremors — serum level), 2021 NEET-PG (haemodialysis useful in lithium overdose), 2023 INI-CET (fine tremors normal), 2022 INI-CET (safe plasma concentration)
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (lithium with coarse tremors — serum level), 20

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Lithium taken in the first trimester is associated with
options: Ebstein anomaly of the tricuspid valve
explanation:
Other classic associations are valproate with neural tube defects, thalidomide with phocomelia, warfarin with nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses, and ACE inhibitors with renal dysgenesis and oligohydramnios.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (lithium — Ebstein anomaly), 2016 AIIMS (lithium — cardiac defects), 2020 INI-CET (match — teratogens)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient with catatonia showing waxy flexibility and mutism is best treated initially with
explanation:
A benzodiazepine challenge is both diagnostic and therapeutic in catatonia. Electroconvulsive therapy is used when it fails. Antipsychotics may worsen catatonia and can precipitate neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (waxy flexibility — lorazepam)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each drug used in substance-use disorders with its mechanism.

| Drug | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Disulfiram | a. Partial agonist at α4β2 nicotinic receptors |
| 2. Acamprosate | b. Inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase |
| 3. Varenicline | c. Partial agonist at µ opioid receptors |
| 4. Buprenorphine | d. Modulates NMDA and GABA transmission, reducing craving |
explanation:
Disulfiram's effect persists for about a week after stopping, because the enzyme must be resynthesised. Varenicline carries a warning about cardiovascular events. Naltrexone is an opioid antagonist used in both alcohol and opioid dependence.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (match — acamprosate, oxazepam, varenicline), 2022 INI-CET (disulfiram mechanism and persistence), 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (varenicline for smoking cessation, 4X), 2023 NEET-PG (buprenorphine maintenance), 2016 AIIMS (detoxification drugs)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: In alcohol withdrawal with impaired liver function, the preferred benzodiazepine is
explanation:
These undergo only glucuronide conjugation (Phase II) and have no active metabolites, so they do not accumulate in liver disease. Thiamine must be given before glucose to avoid precipitating Wernicke encephalopathy.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (delirium tremens — oxazepam), 2020 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (alcohol withdrawal — lorazepam), 2022 INI-CET (alcoholic seizure — IV diazepam and thiamine)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Flumazenil is used for
options: Reversal of benzodiazepine-induced sedation, used cautiously because it can precipitate seizures
explanation:
It is a competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine site. In a patient dependent on benzodiazepines, or who has also taken a tricyclic, reversal can cause status epilepticus. Its short half-life means re-sedation can occur.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (flumazenil for benzodiazepine toxicity), 2022 INI-CET (flumazenil not for alcohol dependence — false), 2016 AIIMS (not used in detoxification)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Naloxone is given by all the following routes in opioid overdose EXCEPT
explanation:
Naloxone has extensive first-pass metabolism, so it is ineffective orally. That property is exploited in fixed combinations where oral naloxone deters misuse while remaining inactive systemically. Its short duration means repeated doses or infusion are needed for long-acting opioids.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (naloxone routes — not oral), 2020 NEET-PG (opioid poisoning — naloxone)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Morphine is traditionally avoided in biliary colic because it
options: Causes spasm of the sphincter of Oddi and raises biliary pressure
explanation:
All opioids do this to some degree, and modern practice allows their use with an antispasmodic. Morphine also causes constipation, to which tolerance does not develop, along with miosis and respiratory depression.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (morphine in biliary colic), 2021 NEET-PG (avoid morphine in biliary colic)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Atropine is added to diphenoxylate in antidiarrhoeal preparations to
options: Discourage misuse by producing unpleasant antimuscarinic effects at higher doses
explanation:
The atropine dose is subtherapeutic at normal use. Loperamide does not cross the blood–brain barrier appreciably, so it has little abuse potential and is preferred, including for chemotherapy-induced diarrhoea.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (atropine with diphenoxylate — prevent abuse), 2019 NEET-PG (chemotherapy diarrhoea — loperamide)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The drug most effective for the motor symptoms of Parkinson disease, and the reason carbidopa is combined with it, are
options: Levodopa; carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase, reducing nausea and increasing brain delivery
explanation:
Carbidopa does not cross the blood–brain barrier. Entacapone inhibits COMT to prolong the levodopa effect. Long-term levodopa causes motor fluctuations and dyskinesias.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (most effective for tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia — levodopa)
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (most effective for tremor, rigidity, bradykine

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each drug used in dementia with its mechanism or special feature.

| Drug | Feature |
|---|---|
| 1. Donepezil | a. NMDA receptor antagonist for moderate to severe disease |
| 2. Memantine | b. Monoclonal antibody against amyloid beta |
| 3. Rivastigmine | c. Long-acting cholinesterase inhibitor given once daily |
| 4. Lecanemab | d. Cholinesterase inhibitor available as a transdermal patch |
explanation:
Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter most reduced in Alzheimer disease. The rivastigmine patch is useful when a patient refuses oral medication. Memantine is often combined with a cholinesterase inhibitor in advanced disease.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (memantine — NMDA antagonist, combination therapy), 2023 INI-CET (refusing oral drug — rivastigmine), 2022 NEET-PG (neurotransmitter reduced in Alzheimer)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The drug of choice for restless legs syndrome presenting with crawling sensations relieved by movement is
explanation:
Iron deficiency should be corrected first, as ferritin below 75 µg/L is a common reversible cause. Dopamine antagonists such as metoclopramide and antidepressants worsen the condition. Gabapentin enacarbil and α2δ ligands avoid the augmentation seen with long-term dopamine agonists.
> `CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (restless legs — gabapentin), 2023 INI-CET (pregabalin in neuropathic pain)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each antiarrhythmic with its Vaughan Williams class and main action.

| Drug | Class and action |
|---|---|
| 1. Quinidine | a. Class II — β blockade |
| 2. Lidocaine | b. Class III — potassium channel blockade |
| 3. Metoprolol | c. Class IB — sodium channel block, shortens action potential |
| 4. Ibutilide | d. Class IA — sodium channel block, prolongs action potential and QT |
explanation:
Quinidine prolongs the QT interval and can cause torsades de pointes. Lidocaine is the drug of choice for digitalis-induced ventricular arrhythmia because it shortens the action potential and acts on ischaemic tissue. Digoxin is not in this classification; it inhibits Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG (match — quinidine, ibutilide, digoxin, 3X), 2023 INI-CET (quinidine prolongs action potential; VT with QT prolongation), 2018 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (digitalis-induced VT — lidocaine)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on long-term amiodarone should be monitored for all of the following EXCEPT
options: Corneal microdeposits and slate-grey skin discoloration
explanation:
Amiodarone is iodine-rich, so both hypothyroidism and thyrotoxicosis occur. It also causes hepatotoxicity and peripheral neuropathy, and is contraindicated in interstitial lung disease. Its half-life is several weeks, so effects persist long after stopping.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (blue-pink skin discoloration — amiodarone), 2023 NEET-PG (pulmonary fibrosis; contraindicated in ILD), 2020 NEET-PG (IV amiodarone for VT)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on digoxin develops nausea, confusion and yellow-green visual halos. The factor most likely to have precipitated this is
explanation:
Potassium competes with digoxin for binding to Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase, so low potassium increases binding and toxicity. Hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia, renal impairment and interacting drugs such as clarithromycin, verapamil and amiodarone also raise levels. Severe toxicity is treated with digoxin-specific antibody fragments.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (digoxin — xanthopsia, hypokalaemia), 2021 NEET-PG (digoxin overdose — immune Fab), 2019 NEET-PG (clarithromycin raising digoxin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: In acute angina, the main benefit of sublingual nitroglycerin comes from
options: Venodilatation that reduces preload and myocardial oxygen demand
explanation:
Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide, which activates guanylyl cyclase and raises cGMP. Sublingual administration avoids extensive first-pass metabolism, and nitroglycerin's lipid solubility allows rapid absorption. Tolerance requires a nitrate-free interval.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (nitrate decreases preload; nitroprusside activates guanylyl cyclase), 2014 AIIMS (sublingual nitroglycerin — lipid soluble), 2016 AIIMS (NO second messenger — cGMP)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A man taking tadalafil for erectile dysfunction presents with chest pain. The drug that must be avoided is
explanation:
Both raise cGMP, and together they cause profound, refractory hypotension. Nitrates should be withheld for 24 hours after sildenafil and 48 hours after tadalafil, which is the longest-acting PDE-5 inhibitor. Sildenafil and tadalafil are also used in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (avoid vasodilators with sildenafil and tadalafil), 2023 NEET-PG (longest-acting PDE inhibitor — tadalafil)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is started on sacubitril–valsartan. Sacubitril acts by
options: Inhibiting neprilysin, so natriuretic peptides are not degraded
explanation:
It must be combined with an ARB rather than an ACE inhibitor, because combining neprilysin and ACE inhibition causes angioedema; a 36-hour washout is required when switching. Omapatrilat inhibited both and was abandoned for that reason.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (sacubitril — neutral endopeptidase inhibitor), 2023 NEET-PG (omapatrilat — ACE and NEP)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The drug classes proven to reduce mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction include all EXCEPT
options: β blockers such as bisoprolol, carvedilol and metoprolol succinate
explanation:
Diuretics relieve congestion and symptoms but do not improve survival. SGLT2 inhibitors such as dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are now the fourth pillar, with benefit regardless of diabetes status.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (nocturnal dyspnoea with cardiomegaly — captopril), 2022 NEET-PG (prevents remodelling, increases longevity — metoprolol/bisoprolol), 2022 INI-CET (empagliflozin/dapagliflozin in HFrEF)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy because they cause
options: Fetal renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios and skull hypoplasia
explanation:
Fetal renal perfusion depends on angiotensin II. Methyldopa, labetalol and nifedipine are the preferred antihypertensives in pregnancy. ACE inhibitors also cause a dry cough from bradykinin accumulation and hyperkalaemia.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (avoid ACE inhibitors in pregnancy), 2016 AIIMS (hypertension with seizures — nifedipine), 2021 INI-CET (avoid losartan in hyperkalaemia)
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (avoid ACE inhibitors in pregnancy), 2016 AIIMS

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A hypertensive patient with type 2 diabetes and albuminuria is best started on
explanation:
These reduce intraglomerular pressure and slow progression of diabetic nephropathy. Telmisartan additionally has partial PPAR-γ agonist activity. Thiazides can worsen glycaemic control and raise urate.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (hypertension with HbA1c >8 — telmisartan), 2015 AIIMS (telmisartan — PPAR-γ), 2020 INI-CET (hydrochlorothiazide not safe in diabetes)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A hypertensive patient with recurrent calcium oxalate stones benefits most from
explanation:
Thiazides increase distal tubular calcium reabsorption and lower urinary calcium. Loop diuretics do the opposite and promote stones. Acetazolamide alkalinises urine and predisposes to calcium phosphate stones.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (hypertension with renal colic — thiazides), 2021 NEET-PG (thiazide acts in DCT)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Verapamil combined with a β blocker is hazardous because the combination can cause
explanation:
Both suppress the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes and reduce contractility. Verapamil also causes constipation and inhibits P-glycoprotein, which raises digoxin levels. Dihydropyridines such as amlodipine do not have this nodal effect.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2016 AIIMS (metoprolol with verapamil — bradycardia and AV block), 2023 INI-CET (verapamil — constipation), 2024 INI-CET (verapamil inhibits ABC efflux)
exam: 2016 AIIMS (metoprolol with verapamil — bradycardia and AV b

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Ranolazine relieves angina without lowering heart rate or blood pressure because it
options: Inhibits the late inward sodium current, reducing calcium overload and diastolic wall tension
explanation:
It is useful when heart rate and blood pressure are already low. It prolongs the QT interval and is metabolised by CYP3A4. Nicorandil, by contrast, is a potassium-channel opener with a nitrate component.
> `CARDIOVASCULAR` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (late inward sodium channel blocker — ranolazine), 2018 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (nicorandil — potassium channel opener)
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (late inward sodium channel blocker — ranolazin

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Heparin produces its anticoagulant effect by
options: Accelerating antithrombin III, which then inactivates thrombin and factor Xa
explanation:
Low-molecular-weight heparins are too short to bridge thrombin, so they act mainly on factor Xa and need no routine monitoring. Protamine reverses unfractionated heparin fully but LMWH only partly.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (heparin acts via antithrombin III), 2024 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (LMWH in cancer-associated thrombosis)
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (heparin acts via antithrombin III

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman at 36 weeks of pregnancy with a prosthetic heart valve is on warfarin. The correct step is
options: Switch to heparin, because it does not cross the placenta
Switch to a direct oral anticoagulant
explanation:
Warfarin crosses the placenta and causes embryopathy in the first trimester (nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses, through effects on osteocalcin) and fetal bleeding near delivery. Direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated in pregnancy and with mechanical valves.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (36 weeks on warfarin — switch to heparin, 4X), 2016 AIIMS (switch at 36 weeks), 2017 AIIMS (warfarin embryopathy — osteocalcin)
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (36 weeks on warfarin — switch to heparin, 4X),

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis in the first days of therapy occurs because
options: Protein C, which has a short half-life, falls before the procoagulant factors, causing a transient prothrombotic state
explanation:
The risk is greatest in people with inherited protein C deficiency, which is why heparin is overlapped with warfarin for at least 5 days. Purple toe syndrome is a separate late complication.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (purple toe and skin necrosis — warfarin), 2014 AIIMS pathology (rat poison and dermal necrosis — protein C deficiency)
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (purple toe and skin necrosis — warfarin), 2014

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Warfarin dose requirements vary between individuals largely because of genetic variation in
explanation:
CYP2C9 metabolises the active S-isomer and VKORC1 is the drug target. CYP2C19 loss-of-function is the reason some patients fail to respond to clopidogrel, which is a prodrug.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (warfarin — CYP2C9 and VKORC1), 2022 INI-CET (clopidogrel failure — CYP2C19)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each antiplatelet or anticoagulant with its mechanism.

| Drug | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Aspirin | a. Direct factor Xa inhibitor |
| 2. Clopidogrel | b. Blocks glycoprotein IIb/IIIa |
| 3. Rivaroxaban | c. Irreversibly inhibits cyclo-oxygenase, reducing thromboxane A2 |
| 4. Tirofiban | d. Irreversibly blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor |
explanation:
Ticagrelor is a reversible P2Y12 blocker that does not need activation. Abciximab and eptifibatide are the other glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors. Andexanet alfa reverses factor Xa inhibitors and idarucizumab reverses dabigatran.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG / 2015 AIIMS (aspirin — thromboxane A2), 2018 AIIMS (ADP receptor blockers), 2023 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (GpIIb/IIIa inhibitors), 2022 NEET-PG / 2016 AIIMS (rivaroxaban), 2020 INI-CET (andexanet alfa)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Alteplase dissolves thrombi by
options: Converting plasminogen to plasmin, preferentially on fibrin-bound plasminogen
explanation:
This fibrin selectivity limits systemic fibrinogen depletion compared with streptokinase. The opposite effect is produced by tranexamic acid and aminocaproic acid, which block the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (tPA — enhances fibrin degradation), 2018 NEET-PG / 2015 AIIMS (aminocaproic acid — antifibrinolytic)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Oral iron absorption is best when the tablet is taken
options: On an empty stomach, with vitamin C
explanation:
Ascorbate reduces ferric to the better-absorbed ferrous form. Phytates, tannins in tea, calcium, antacids and proton pump inhibitors reduce absorption. In iron poisoning, the chelator is desferrioxamine; dimercaprol is contraindicated because its iron complex is itself toxic.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (vitamin C increases iron absorption), 2023 NEET-PG (desferrioxamine), 2023 NEET-PG (BAL contraindicated in iron poisoning), 2022 INI-CET (serum iron >500 µg/dL)
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (vitamin C increases iron absorption), 2023 NEE

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Erythropoietin is most clearly indicated for anaemia due to
explanation:
Iron stores must be adequate first, or the response fails. Over-correction of haemoglobin raises the risk of hypertension, thrombosis and stroke, so a target below normal is used. Oprelvekin (IL-11) is used for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia and filgrastim for neutropenia.
> `BLOOD AND COAGULATION` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (erythropoietin in CKD anaemia, 2X), 2023 NEET-PG (oprelvekin), 2022 NEET-PG (filgrastim)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each oral antidiabetic class with its mechanism.

| Class | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Metformin | a. Inhibits DPP-4, raising GLP-1 and GIP |
| 2. Sitagliptin | b. Activates PPAR-γ, improving insulin sensitivity |
| 3. Pioglitazone | c. Blocks renal sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 |
| 4. Dapagliflozin | d. Activates AMP kinase and reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis |
explanation:
Sulfonylureas close the ATP-sensitive potassium channel on β cells and cause hypoglycaemia and weight gain. Metformin, DPP-4 inhibitors and SGLT2 inhibitors do not cause hypoglycaemia when used alone.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (sitagliptin raises GIP and GLP-1), 2023 NEET-PG (pioglitazone), 2023 INI-CET (dapagliflozin and UTI), 2015 AIIMS (rosiglitazone does not increase insulin secretion)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (sitagliptin raises GIP and GLP-1), 2023 NEET-P

subject: Pharmacology
stem: An SGLT2 inhibitor is particularly indicated, independent of glycaemic control, in a patient with
options: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction or chronic kidney disease
explanation:
Cardiorenal benefit is now the main reason for prescribing them. Adverse effects include genital mycotic infections, urinary infection, volume depletion, euglycaemic ketoacidosis and rarely Fournier gangrene.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (empagliflozin/dapagliflozin in HFrEF), 2020 INI-CET (canagliflozin — vulvovaginal itching; SGLT2 side effects)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The antidiabetic that needs NO dose reduction in advanced renal impairment is
explanation:
Linagliptin is excreted mainly through the bile. Metformin is stopped when eGFR falls below 30 because of lactic acidosis risk, which is also increased by advanced age, liver disease and hypoxia. Metformin additionally causes B12 malabsorption and unexplained diarrhoea.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (linagliptin in CKD), 2022 NEET-PG (no dose reduction in renal failure), 2016 AIIMS (metformin lactic acidosis risk factors), 2023 INI-CET (metformin and diarrhoea)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A child with type 1 diabetes presents with ketoacidosis and a blood glucose of 400 mg/dL. The correct first step is
options: Normal saline in the first hour, then an insulin infusion
explanation:
Fluid is given first because these children are markedly volume depleted, and starting insulin too early worsens the shift of fluid and potassium. Potassium is added once urine output is confirmed, and bicarbonate is reserved for extreme acidosis.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (type 1 diabetes with acidosis — saline then insulin infusion)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (type 1 diabetes with acidosis — saline then in

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for long-term weight management is
explanation:
GLP-1 agonists slow gastric emptying and reduce appetite centrally. Semaglutide and tirzepatide have larger effects. Adverse effects are nausea, pancreatitis and gallstones, and they are avoided in medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN 2.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (liraglutide for long-term obesity treatment)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which drug REDUCES bone resorption rather than stimulating bone formation?
explanation:
Bisphosphonates, denosumab, raloxifene and oestrogen are antiresorptive. Teriparatide is anabolic when given intermittently, but continuous exposure increases resorption, and long use has been linked to osteosarcoma in animals. Oral bisphosphonates are taken on an empty stomach with water, sitting upright.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (drugs decreasing bone resorption — not teriparatide, 3X), 2023 INI-CET (teriparatide and osteosarcoma), 2015 AIIMS (bisphosphonates on empty stomach)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient in thyroid storm should receive all of the following EXCEPT
options: Propylthiouracil, then iodine at least an hour later
explanation:
Aspirin displaces thyroid hormone from thyroid-binding globulin and raises free hormone levels, so paracetamol is used instead. Propylthiouracil is preferred in storm because it also blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion. Iodine must follow the thionamide to avoid fuelling hormone synthesis.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (thyroid storm — propranolol, Lugol's iodine, acetaminophen, not aspirin), 2016 AIIMS (thionamide side effects)
exam: 2022 INI-CET (thyroid storm — propranolol, Lugol's iodine, a

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Propylthiouracil rather than carbimazole is preferred in the first trimester of pregnancy because carbimazole is associated with
explanation:
PTU carries a greater risk of hepatotoxicity, so it is used only in the first trimester and then changed. Both drugs can cause agranulocytosis, and patients are told to report sore throat and fever immediately.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (8-week pregnancy with hyperthyroidism — propylthiouracil), 2016 AIIMS (thionamide adverse effects)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on long-term oral prednisolone for rheumatoid arthritis stops it abruptly and collapses with hypotension, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia. The immediate treatment is
explanation:
Suppression of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis means endogenous cortisol cannot rise. Steroids given for more than 2–3 weeks must be tapered. Topical steroid side effects include skin atrophy, striae, telangiectasia and hypertrichosis.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (sudden stop of steroid — hydrocortisone), 2024 INI-CET (topical steroid side effects)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturation are given as
options: Betamethasone 12 mg intramuscularly, two doses 24 hours apart, or dexamethasone 6 mg 12-hourly for four doses
explanation:
Betamethasone and dexamethasone cross the placenta readily because they are not inactivated by placental 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, unlike hydrocortisone and prednisolone.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (dexamethasone 6 mg 12-hourly, four doses)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman with chronic hypertension develops postpartum haemorrhage. The uterotonic that must be AVOIDED is
explanation:
Ergot alkaloids cause generalised vasoconstriction and can precipitate hypertensive crisis and stroke. Carboprost (a PGF2α analogue) is avoided in asthma because it causes bronchospasm. Oxytocin is avoided in significant cardiac disease because of its vasodilator and antidiuretic effects.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (hypertension with headache — avoid methylergometrine), 2023 NEET-PG (asthma with PPH — avoid carboprost), 2021 NEET-PG (oxytocin avoided in heart disease)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Magnesium sulphate in severe pre-eclampsia should be withheld or stopped when
options: Respiratory rate is above 16 per minute
Patellar reflexes are absent, respiration is below 12 per minute, or urine output is below 30 mL/hour
explanation:
Loss of the patellar reflex is the earliest warning. Magnesium is renally excreted, so oliguria causes accumulation. The antidote is intravenous calcium gluconate. Magnesium is also fetal neuroprotective in preterm labour.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (MgSO4 neuroprotective, reduces seizures), 2023 NEET-PG (indication to stop MgSO4 — urine output)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman whose newborn has died wishes to suppress lactation. The appropriate drug is
explanation:
Cabergoline is a long-acting dopamine D2 agonist that suppresses prolactin. It is also the drug of choice for prolactinoma, where it shrinks the tumour. Metoclopramide and domperidone block D2 receptors and therefore raise prolactin.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (suppress lactation — cabergoline), 2020 NEET-PG (pituitary adenoma — cabergoline)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Pegvisomant is used in acromegaly that is resistant to other treatment. It acts as
explanation:
It lowers IGF-1 but not GH levels, so IGF-1 is used for monitoring, and it does not shrink the tumour. Octreotide and lanreotide are somatostatin analogues that do reduce both GH and tumour size.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (pegvisomant — GH receptor blocker), 2021 NEET-PG (lanreotide depot for acromegaly)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Finasteride reduces prostate size in benign prostatic hyperplasia by
explanation:
It takes 3–6 months to work, roughly halves the PSA value, and causes sexual dysfunction. α blockers relieve symptoms within days by relaxing smooth muscle, so the two are often combined.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (5α-reductase inhibitor — decrease intracellular DHT)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Metyrapone is used in the investigation and treatment of Cushing syndrome because it inhibits
options: 11β-hydroxylase, the last step of cortisol synthesis
explanation:
Ketoconazole also blocks steroidogenesis at several steps, and mifepristone blocks the glucocorticoid receptor. Etomidate inhibits the same enzyme as metyrapone, which explains its adrenal suppression.
> `ENDOCRINE AND REPRODUCTIVE` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (metyrapone inhibits glucocorticoid synthesis), 2024 INI-CET (etomidate and adrenal insufficiency)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The analgesic of choice for a patient with end-stage renal disease on dialysis is
explanation:
NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin-dependent afferent arteriolar dilatation and worsen renal function, and also raise cardiovascular and gastrointestinal risk. In paracetamol overdose, N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and neutralises NAPQI.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG (analgesic in renal failure on dialysis — acetaminophen), 2020 NEET-PG (paracetamol overdose — N-acetylcysteine)
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (analgesic in renal failure on dialysis — aceta

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman at 32 weeks of pregnancy is given indomethacin for polyhydramnios. The main fetal risk is
options: Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
explanation:
Prostaglandins keep the ductus open, so NSAIDs close it; the same mechanism is used therapeutically with indomethacin or ibuprofen to close a patent ductus in preterm babies. Prostaglandin E1 (alprostadil) keeps it open in duct-dependent heart disease.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG (indomethacin in pregnancy — premature closure of ductus), 2016 AIIMS (misoprostol — PGE1)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: An asthmatic develops wheeze, rhinorrhoea and nasal polyps after taking aspirin. This reaction is
options: An IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity reaction
Due to shunting of arachidonic acid down the lipoxygenase pathway, increasing leukotrienes
A type III immune complex reaction
explanation:
This is aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, which is pharmacological and not allergic, so all non-selective COX inhibitors cross-react. Leukotriene modifiers such as montelukast and zileuton are useful.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (aspirin wheeze — not type I hypersensitivity)
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (aspirin wheeze — not type I hypersensitivity)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: In an acute attack of gout, colchicine relieves pain by
options: Binding tubulin and preventing neutrophil migration and NLRP3 inflammasome activation
explanation:
Colchicine has no effect on urate levels. Its dose-limiting adverse effect is diarrhoea, and it causes metaphase arrest. NSAIDs and short-course steroids are the other options for an acute attack.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (colchicine — neutrophil migration, metaphase arrest, 2X)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Starting allopurinol during an acute attack of gout is avoided because
options: It has no effect on urate
A sudden fall in serum urate mobilises crystals and can prolong or worsen the attack
explanation:
Urate-lowering therapy is started after the attack settles, under cover of colchicine or an NSAID. Allopurinol and febuxostat inhibit xanthine oxidase; probenecid and benzbromarone are uricosuric and avoided when there are urate stones.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 NEET-PG (xanthine oxidase inhibition — allopurinol), 2023 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (febuxostat for gout), 2021 NEET-PG (probenecid), 2017 AIIMS (uricosuric drugs)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Allopurinol markedly increases the toxicity of which drug, requiring a large dose reduction?
explanation:
Azathioprine is converted to 6-mercaptopurine, which is inactivated by xanthine oxidase. Blocking that enzyme causes severe myelosuppression. Azathioprine toxicity also shows as raised transaminases, and TPMT deficiency is a separate cause.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (liver enzyme raised in azathioprine toxicity), 2023 INI-CET (azathioprine not first-line in rheumatoid arthritis)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient with migraine and known coronary artery disease develops chest pain after taking a triptan. The mechanism is
explanation:
Triptans are contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension and hemiplegic migraine. Ergot alkaloids are even more strongly vasoconstrictive and can cause ergotism with limb ischaemia; the newer CGRP antagonists avoid this.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (migraine with CAD, chest pain — 5-HT1B/1D agonist), 2022 NEET-PG (sumatriptan for migraine), 2021 INI-CET (ergotism)
exam: 2020 INI-CET (migraine with CAD, chest pain — 5-HT1B/1D agon

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which antihistamine carries the greatest risk of torsades de pointes when combined with erythromycin?
explanation:
Astemizole and terfenadine block cardiac potassium channels, and erythromycin inhibits their metabolism, so both were withdrawn. Fexofenadine is the safe active metabolite of terfenadine. Promethazine, a sedating antihistamine, is used for motion sickness.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (astemizole with erythromycin — torsades), 2018 NEET-PG (promethazine for motion sickness)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient in the emergency department with severe asthma is given nebulised salbutamol and intravenous hydrocortisone. Steroids help in this setting mainly by
options: Reducing airway inflammation and upregulating β2 receptors, with benefit over hours
explanation:
Steroids are not bronchodilators but are essential in acute severe asthma. Salbutamol causes tremor, tachycardia, hypokalaemia and hyperglycaemia. Inhaled steroids predispose to oral candidiasis, which is reduced by rinsing the mouth.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (useful in asthma but not bronchodilator — hydrocortisone), 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (salbutamol side effects, 4X), 2014 AIIMS (steroids facilitate β agonists), 2023 NEET-PG (inhaled steroid thrush — clotrimazole)
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (useful in asthma but not bronchodilator — hydr

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Theophylline should not be combined with erythromycin or ciprofloxacin because these drugs
options: Inhibit CYP1A2 and raise theophylline levels towards toxicity
explanation:
Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index, causing nausea, arrhythmia and seizures. It inhibits phosphodiesterase (causing gastrointestinal upset through PDE4) and antagonises adenosine receptors, which explains its diuretic effect and the wakefulness caused by caffeine.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2021 NEET-PG (antibiotic not combined with theophylline — erythromycin), 2018 AIIMS (GI discomfort — PDE4), 2020 NEET-PG (diuresis — adenosine A1 antagonism), 2019 NEET-PG (caffeine — adenosine antagonism)
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (antibiotic not combined with theophylline — er

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Omalizumab is used in severe allergic asthma. It acts by
options: Binding free IgE and preventing it from attaching to mast cell FcεRI receptors
explanation:
Mepolizumab and benralizumab target the IL-5 pathway in eosinophilic asthma, and dupilumab targets IL-4Rα. These biologics are reserved for severe disease uncontrolled on inhaled therapy.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (IgE antagonist — omalizumab)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Prokinetic drugs used in gastroparesis include all of the following mechanisms EXCEPT
explanation:
Antimuscarinics slow gut motility. Metoclopramide and domperidone are D2 blockers, prucalopride is a 5-HT4 agonist, and erythromycin acts on motilin receptors. Metoclopramide crosses into the brain and causes dystonia; domperidone does not.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (prokinetics — 5-HT4 agonist, D2 blocker, macrolides), 2022 INI-CET (prucalopride — 5-HT4 agonist), 2024 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (metoclopramide and abnormal posturing), 2018 AIIMS (metoclopramide — D2 antagonism)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on phenytoin is also prescribed sucralfate. The two should be separated by about 2 hours because sucralfate
options: Binds phenytoin in the gut and reduces its absorption
explanation:
Sucralfate forms a viscous polymer that also chelates other drugs, including fluoroquinolones, digoxin and levothyroxine. Antacids and iron behave similarly, so timing matters.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (minimum gap between phenytoin and sucralfate — 120 min)
exam: 2024 INI-CET (minimum gap between phenytoin and sucralfate —

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Acetazolamide helps in acute mountain sickness by
options: Causing a bicarbonate diuresis and metabolic acidosis, which stimulates ventilation
explanation:
It acts on carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule and offsets the respiratory alkalosis of hypoxic hyperventilation. Immediate descent and oxygen remain the definitive measures. Dorzolamide is the topical form used in glaucoma.
> `AUTACOIDS AND OTHERS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (altitude sickness — descent, oxygen, acetazolamide, 3X), 2021 INI-CET (carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act in proximal tubule), 2017 AIIMS (acetazolamide, dorzolamide)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each antibacterial with its mechanism of action.

| Drug | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Vancomycin | a. Inhibits DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) |
| 2. Ciprofloxacin | b. Binds the 50S subunit and blocks formation of the initiation complex |
| 3. Linezolid | c. Binds D-alanyl-D-alanine and blocks cell wall cross-linking |
| 4. Gentamicin | d. Binds the 30S subunit, causing misreading of mRNA |
explanation:
Vancomycin resistance in enterococci comes from replacing the terminal D-alanine with D-lactate. Linezolid's unique binding site means no cross-resistance with other protein synthesis inhibitors.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (binds D-ala-D-ala — vancomycin), 2019 NEET-PG (DNA gyrase — ciprofloxacin), 2016 AIIMS (protein synthesis inhibitors)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Aminoglycosides are ineffective against anaerobic organisms because
options: They are destroyed by low pH
Their uptake into the cell requires oxygen-dependent active transport
explanation:
The same reason explains poor activity in abscesses and acidic environments. Aminoglycosides show concentration-dependent killing with a post-antibiotic effect, which is why once-daily dosing is used, and they cause nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (aminoglycosides do not act on anaerobes), 2015 AIIMS (drugs causing hearing loss)
exam: 2019 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (aminoglycosides do not act on ana

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Imipenem is combined with cilastatin because cilastatin
options: Inhibits renal dehydropeptidase I, which would otherwise degrade imipenem in the tubule
explanation:
Cilastatin has no antibacterial activity. Imipenem has the highest seizure risk among carbapenems; meropenem is preferred in CNS infection. Ertapenem does not cover *Pseudomonas*, *Acinetobacter* or *Enterococcus*.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2018 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (cilastatin and renal enzyme), 2019 NEET-PG / 2018 AIIMS (imipenem — maximum seizures)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which antibiotic is NOT active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus?
explanation:
Methicillin resistance is due to altered PBP2a, so **all** β-lactams fail, including carbapenems, regardless of β-lactamase inhibitors. Ceftaroline is the exception among cephalosporins. Daptomycin is inactivated by surfactant, so it cannot be used in pneumonia.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (MRSA also resistant to piperacillin), 2020 INI-CET (meropenem not for MRSA), 2016 AIIMS (daptomycin killing)
exam: 2020 INI-CET (MRSA also resistant to piperacillin), 2020 INI

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on chemotherapy with pancytopenia develops a resistant Gram-positive infection. The antibiotic to use with caution is
explanation:
Thrombocytopenia is the commonest effect and is related to treatment beyond 2 weeks. Linezolid is also a weak MAO inhibitor, so it can cause serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, and prolonged use causes optic and peripheral neuropathy and lactic acidosis.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET (avoid in chemotherapy with pancytopenia — linezolid)
exam: 2020 INI-CET (avoid in chemotherapy with pancytopenia — line

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which antimicrobial is relatively contraindicated in a patient with epilepsy?
explanation:
Fluoroquinolones antagonise GABA-A and lower the seizure threshold. They also cause tendinitis and tendon rupture, QT prolongation, dysglycaemia and aortic aneurysm, and are avoided in children and pregnancy because of cartilage toxicity. Levofloxacin has the highest oral bioavailability.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `New-adjacent` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 NEET-PG (contraindicated in seizure disorder — ciprofloxacin), 2020 NEET-PG (tendon rupture and arthropathy), 2020 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (levofloxacin bioavailability), 2020 NEET-PG (pefloxacin in liver disease)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A woman in the third trimester is given cotrimoxazole. The risk to the newborn is
options: Kernicterus from displacement of bilirubin from albumin
explanation:
Sulfonamides are avoided near term for this reason, and in the first trimester because trimethoprim is a folate antagonist. Chloramphenicol causes grey baby syndrome, tetracyclines discolour teeth, and fluoroquinolones affect cartilage.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (third trimester drug raising newborn bilirubin — cotrimoxazole)
exam: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (third trimester drug raising newb

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Azithromycin is preferred to erythromycin for outpatient community-acquired pneumonia mainly because it
options: Has a much longer half-life with high tissue concentrations, allowing short once-daily courses
Has no gastrointestinal effects at all
explanation:
Azithromycin is also a much weaker CYP3A4 inhibitor than erythromycin and clarithromycin, so it has fewer interactions. Macrolides can prolong the QT interval. Erythromycin is the drug of choice for the diphtheria carrier state.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (community-acquired pneumonia in OPD — azithromycin), 2017 AIIMS (diphtheria carrier — erythromycin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Clindamycin is added to a β-lactam in streptococcal toxic shock syndrome because it
options: Suppresses toxin production by inhibiting protein synthesis, and works even when organisms are not dividing
explanation:
β-lactams are less effective against a dense, stationary-phase inoculum (the Eagle effect). Clindamycin also achieves high bone concentrations, but carries the highest risk of *C. difficile* colitis.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `New-adjacent` • `Hard` • Based on: 2015 AIIMS (toxic shock syndrome — clindamycin), 2016 AIIMS (high bone concentration — clindamycin)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: The combination of a β-lactam with a β-lactamase inhibitor is effective against ESBL-producing Klebsiella in mild infection because the inhibitor
options: Binds and inactivates the β-lactamase enzyme, protecting the partner antibiotic
explanation:
For serious ESBL infections, carbapenems remain the standard. Bacterial resistance arises by enzyme production, altered target, reduced porin permeability and active efflux.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2017 AIIMS (ESBL Klebsiella — β-lactam with inhibitor), 2018 NEET-PG (β-lactamase destroys drug structure), 2017 AIIMS / 2016 AIIMS (mechanisms of resistance)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: First-line treatment for a complicated urinary tract infection with septic shock, pending cultures, is
explanation:
Broad empirical cover is needed in septic shock, with de-escalation once sensitivities are known. Nitrofurantoin reaches therapeutic levels only in urine, so it is unsuitable for pyelonephritis or systemic infection.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2023 INI-CET (complicated UTI with septic shock — meropenem), 2020 INI-CET (meropenem indications)
exam: 2023 INI-CET (complicated UTI with septic shock — meropenem)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each first-line antitubercular drug with its characteristic adverse effect.

| Drug | Adverse effect |
|---|---|
| 1. Isoniazid | a. Hyperuricaemia and arthralgia |
| 2. Rifampicin | b. Retrobulbar neuritis with loss of red–green discrimination |
| 3. Pyrazinamide | c. Peripheral neuropathy, prevented by pyridoxine |
| 4. Ethambutol | d. Orange discoloration of secretions and enzyme induction |
explanation:
Isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis and needs activation by the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG; resistance often involves katG mutations. If asymptomatic hyperuricaemia occurs on ATT, pyrazinamide is usually continued unless arthritis is troublesome.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (ethambutol — ocular effects), 2021 INI-CET (isoniazid — mycolic acid via catalase), 2022 INI-CET (raised uric acid on ATT), 2021 NEET-PG (ATT neuropathy — vitamin B6), 2016 AIIMS (isoniazid side effects)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: An HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 80 is newly diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis. The correct sequence is
options: Start antiretroviral therapy first, then antitubercular treatment after 8 weeks
Start both on the same day
Start antitubercular treatment first, and add antiretroviral therapy within 2 weeks
Treat tuberculosis fully before starting antiretrovirals
explanation:
Early ART improves survival at low CD4 counts, but starting both together increases immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome. Rifampicin induces CYP3A4 and lowers protease inhibitor levels, so rifabutin is substituted or doses adjusted.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Hard` • Based on: 2021 INI-CET (when to start ATT in HIV), 2022 NEET-PG (which ATT drug to change on nevirapine)
exam: 2021 INI-CET (when to start ATT in HIV), 2022 NEET-PG (which

subject: Pharmacology
stem: A patient on second-line antitubercular treatment develops weight gain, cold intolerance and a raised TSH with low T4. The likely drug is
explanation:
Ethionamide and para-aminosalicylic acid both cause hypothyroidism, which is reversible on stopping. Bedaquiline inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase and prolongs the QT interval. Linezolid causes myelosuppression and neuropathy.
> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 INI-CET (MDR-TB with hypothyroidism — ethionamide), 2021 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (bedaquiline — ATP synthase)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Dapsone, used in leprosy, acts by

explanation:

explanation:

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Which antiretroviral is also effective against hepatitis B, making it useful in co-infection?
explanation:

stem: The drug of choice for invasive aspergillosis is
explanation:

> `ANTIMICROBIALS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2022 NEET-PG (DOC invasive aspergillosis — voriconazole), 2022 NEET-PG / 2017 AIIMS (amphotericin mechanism), 2022 NEET-PG (cryptococcal meningitis — liposomal amphotericin with flucytosine)

subject: Pharmacology
stem:
Match each cytotoxic drug with its characteristic dose-limiting toxicity.

| Drug | Toxicity |
|---|---|
| 1. Bleomycin | a. Haemorrhagic cystitis |
| 2. Doxorubicin | b. Peripheral neuropathy |
| 3. Cyclophosphamide | c. Pulmonary fibrosis and flagellate skin pigmentation |
| 4. Vincristine | d. Dilated cardiomyopathy |
explanation:
Bleomycin causes little myelosuppression. Capecitabine causes hand–foot syndrome, and cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and severe emesis. Vinca alkaloids inhibit microtubule polymerisation; taxanes prevent depolymerisation.
> `ANTICANCER AND IMMUNOMODULATORS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (flagellate pigmentation — bleomycin), 2024 INI-CET (match — capecitabine hand–foot), 2014 AIIMS (vinca alkaloids — microtubule polymerisation)

subject: Pharmacology
stem: Haemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide is caused by its metabolite acrolein and is prevented by
explanation:

> `ANTICANCER AND IMMUNOMODULATORS` • `Reworded` • `Moderate` • Based on: 2024 INI-CET (daunorubicin cardiotoxicity prevented by dexrazoxane), 2023 INI-CET (active metabolite of cyclophosphamide), 2020 NEET-PG (cyclophosphamide — DNA cross-linking)

explanation:

stem: PARP inhibitors such as olaparib are most effective in tumours with
